dossiers.name: Classical GRB observations and distance-scale era
dossiers.defining_problem: What are gamma-ray bursts and how far away are they? From the Vela discovery of sixteen 0.2-1.5 MeV bursts of cosmic origin [1973ApJ...182L..85K], this community pursued the phenomenology of the bursts — time structure, energy spectra, sky positions, logN-logS statistics — with the distance scale as the organizing question. KONUS statistics of 85 bursts were read as "proof of a galactic localization" with neutron-star sources [1981Ap&SS..75...47M], while BATSE's isotropic yet inhomogeneous distribution of 153 bursts was "inconsistent with any known population of galactic objects" and pointed to cosmological distances [1992Natur.355..143M], culminating in the 1995 75th-anniversary debate between the cosmological [1995PASP..107.1167P] and Galactic-corona [1995PASP..107.1152L] positions.

The 1979 March 5 event from a flaring X-ray pulsar in Dorado (later SGR 0526-66), repeating on March 6 [1979Natur.282..587M; 1995PASP..107.1152L]

KONUS catalog bursts from Venera 11/12, Sept 1978 - May 1979 (85 events; several types differing in profile, duration, spectrum; repeating short-burst sources) [1981Ap&SS..80....3M; 1981Ap&SS..75...47M]

Short (<2 s, harder) and long (>2 s, softer) burst classes from the first BATSE catalog [1993ApJ...413L.101K]
Bursts with reported cyclotron/annihilation spectral lines (Venera, Ginga, ISEE 3) [1981Natur.290..378M; 1988Natur.335..234M; 1980ApJ...236L..67T]

ISEE 3 radiatively cooled germanium spectrometer [1980ApJ...236L..67T]
Ginga burst spectra [1988Natur.335..234M]
BATSE on the Compton Gamma Ray Observatory: Large Area Detectors for catalogs/statistics, Spectroscopy Detectors for line searches [1992Natur.355..143M; 1993ApJ...413L.101K; 1994ApJ...433L..77P]
characteristic_methods: Multi-spacecraft coincidence detection and triangulation of burst arrival directions [1973ApJ...182L..85K; 1973ApJ...185L..57W; 1975ApJ...196L..43C]
Time-profile and spectral-evolution analysis over keV-MeV bands [1974ApJ...194L..19M; 1973ApJ...185L...1C; 1981Ap&SS..80....3M]
logN-logS (number vs. intensity) statistics tested against the -3/2 Euclidean-homogeneous law, plus V/Vmax [1979SvAL....5...87M; 1992Natur.355..143M; 1995MNRAS.273..755P]
Angular (dipole/quadrupole) isotropy tests of burst sky positions [1992Natur.355..143M; 1995PASP..107.1167P; 1995MNRAS.273..755P]
Spectral-line searches (visual and Bayesian) in burst spectra [1980ApJ...236L..67T; 1981Natur.290..378M; 1994ApJ...433L..77P]
Duration-distribution and hardness-ratio classification [1993ApJ...413L.101K]
Monte Carlo population modeling of Galactic halo/corona source distributions [1995MNRAS.273..755P]
recurring_models: Galactic neutron-star models: strongly magnetized neutron stars evidenced by cyclotron/annihilation lines [1981Natur.290..378M], accreting neutron-star binaries with non-stationary accretion or thermonuclear fusion [1981Ap&SS..75...47M]

High-velocity neutron stars in an extended Galactic halo/corona reproducing BATSE isotropy, requiring >600-700 km/s kicks, >10^9 yr active lifetimes, and possibly magnetar fields ~10^15 G [1995MNRAS.273..755P; 1995PASP..107.1152L]
Cosmological sources at z~1 with ~10^51 erg isotropic energies, e.g. decay of a black-hole/neutron-star binary [1991AcA....41..257P]
Characteristic empirical spectral form: ~150 keV exponential plus power-law tail, common to all bursts [1973ApJ...185L...1C; 1975ApJ...196L..43C]
shaping_results: Discovery of sixteen cosmic gamma-ray bursts with Vela, eliminating the Earth and Sun as sources [1973ApJ...182L..85K]
Confirmation of the hard-spectrum nature of bursts with peak energy release at several hundred keV and a common exponential-plus-power-law spectrum [1973ApJ...185L...1C; 1975ApJ...196L..43C]
The 1979 March 5 super-burst and its recurrence, the first observational link between bursts and neutron stars [1979Natur.282..587M; 1981Ap&SS..75...47M]
KONUS catalogs of burst time structure, spectra, and source coordinates, and the claim of galactic localization from logN-logS and anisotropy [1981Ap&SS..80....3M; 1981Ap&SS..75...47M]
Reported cyclotron and annihilation lines as evidence for strongly magnetized neutron stars [1981Natur.290..378M; 1988Natur.335..234M; 1980ApJ...236L..67T]
BATSE's isotropic-but-inhomogeneous distribution of 153 bursts, inconsistent with any known galactic population [1992Natur.355..143M]
Identification of the short/long burst dichotomy at 2 s with duration-hardness anticorrelation [1993ApJ...413L.101K]
BATSE Spectroscopy Detector non-detection of narrow lines in 192 bursts, undermining the cyclotron-line evidence [1994ApJ...433L..77P]
internal_disagreements: Galactic vs. cosmological distance scale: KONUS analyses claimed proof of galactic localization from logN-logS and source anisotropy [1981Ap&SS..75...47M], whereas BATSE found isotropy plus a non -3/2 logN-logS inconsistent with any known galactic population and suggestive of cosmological distances [1992Natur.355..143M]; the dispute was formalized in the 1995 debate, Paczynski arguing the cosmological case [1995PASP..107.1167P; 1991AcA....41..257P] against Lamb's Galactic corona of high-velocity neutron stars anchored on the 1979 March 5 event at 50 kpc [1995PASP..107.1152L], with halo modelers showing non-spherical halos could still mimic BATSE isotropy at the cost of >600-700 km/s kicks and >10^9 yr lifetimes [1995MNRAS.273..755P]

Reality of spectral lines: Venera/KONUS reported cyclotron and annihilation lines as a characteristic rather than exceptional feature and the most convincing evidence for magnetized neutron stars [1981Natur.290..378M], supported by Ginga cyclotron absorption features [1988Natur.335..234M] and ISEE 3 features at ~420 and ~740 keV [1980ApJ...236L..67T]; but early IMP-6 spectra showed no evidence of line structure [1973ApJ...185L...1C], and BATSE found no convincing narrow lines in 192 bursts, in explicit contrast to Ginga expectations (consistency only at the 13% level) [1994ApJ...433L..77P]

Interpretation of the logN-logS deficit: the same departure from the -3/2 law seen by KONUS/Cone [1979SvAL....5...87M] was read as evidence for a bounded galactic disk population [1981Ap&SS..75...47M] and later as evidence for a cosmological population with the observer at the center of a bounded spherical distribution [1992Natur.355..143M; 1995PASP..107.1167P]
dossiers.activity: Founded with the 1973 Vela discovery [1973ApJ...182L..85K], with a first observational wave in 1973-1975 (IMP, OSO-7, Apollo) [1973ApJ...185L..57W; 1974ApJ...194L..19M; 1975ApJ...196L..43C], a second in 1979-1981 (Venera/KONUS, ISEE 3) [1979Natur.282..587M; 1981Ap&SS..80....3M; 1980ApJ...236L..67T], and its peak in the BATSE era of the early-to-mid 1990s (median year 1995) around the distance-scale debate [1992Natur.355..143M; 1995PASP..107.1167P; 1995PASP..107.1152L]. The community is essentially historical: its central question was settled for the cosmological scale, with galactic halo models retrospectively noted as ruled out by afterglow and host-galaxy observations [1995MNRAS.273..755P].

dossiers.name: GRB Afterglow Fireball Physics
dossiers.defining_problem: What powers gamma-ray bursts and their multiwavelength afterglows, and at what distance? The community formed around the relativistic fireball external-shock idea — that a fireball's expansion energy is reconverted to radiation when it decelerates in an external medium [1992MNRAS.258P..41R] — which predicted long-lived optical, X-ray, and radio emission fading as power laws [1997ApJ...476..232M; 1993ApJ...418L...5P]. The 1997 BeppoSAX-enabled discoveries of the first X-ray afterglow [1997Natur.387..783C], the first optical transient [1997Natur.386..686V], the first redshift [1997Natur.387..878M], and the first radio afterglow [1997Natur.389..261F] converted these predictions into an observational program: use afterglow spectra and light curves to test blast-wave physics and infer burst energetics, geometry, and environments [1997MNRAS.288L..51W; 1998ApJ...497L..17S; 1999ApJ...519L..17S].
populations_events: GRB 970228 — first X-ray afterglow (8 hr after burst, power-law decay) and first fading optical transient associated with a faint galaxy [1997Natur.387..783C; 1997Natur.386..686V]

GRB 970508 — first redshift limit (0.835 <= z <~ 2.3 from absorption spectroscopy) and first radio afterglow, with scintillation giving a ~3 microarcsecond source size [1997Natur.387..878M; 1997Natur.389..261F]
GRB 970402 — early X-ray/optical afterglow used with 970228 to constrain fireball-model parameters [1997ApJ...485L...5W]
GRB 980519 — rapid t^(-2.05±0.04) optical/X-ray decay taken as evidence for a jet [1999ApJ...519L..17S]
GRBs 990123 and 990510 — afterglows favoring constant-density interstellar interaction [2000ApJ...536..195C]
GRB 980425/SN 1998bw and GRBs 980326, 980519 — afterglows explained by stellar-wind interaction, tying bursts to massive-star progenitors [2000ApJ...536..195C]
The long-burst population as a whole, whose isotropic sky distribution but inhomogeneous spatial distribution framed the distance-scale problem [1997Natur.387..783C; 1990ApJ...348..485P]
The bimodal burst-duration distribution, tentatively attributed to Newtonian vs relativistic reverse shocks [1995ApJ...455L.143S]
instruments_datasets: BeppoSAX (SAX) satellite — Wide Field Cameras for rapid localization and narrow-field X-ray follow-up; the PDS high-energy instrument (15-300 keV, 800 cm^2 phoswich) with CsI shields doubling as a GRB monitor [1991AdSpR..11h.281F; 1997Natur.387..783C; 1997MNRAS.288L..51W]
Ground-based optical telescopes performing rapid error-box imaging within ~21 hours of a burst [1997Natur.386..686V]
Optical spectrographs delivering absorption-line redshifts of afterglow transients [1997Natur.387..878M]
Radio interferometric monitoring of afterglows, including interstellar-scintillation 'twinkling' as a size probe [1997Natur.389..261F; 1993ApJ...418L...5P]
Multiwavelength (gamma-ray to radio) follow-up campaigns triggered by rapid burst localizations [1997Natur.387..783C; 1997Natur.389..261F]
characteristic_methods: Analytical relativistic blast-wave / fireball shock dynamics for energy conversion timescales and deceleration [1992MNRAS.258P..41R; 1995ApJ...455L.143S]

Synchrotron spectral and light-curve modeling with power-law electron distributions, yielding explicit spectral-index/temporal-index relations (closure relations) [1998ApJ...497L..17S; 1997ApJ...485L...5W]
Power-law fitting of multiwavelength afterglow decays to test blast-wave predictions [1997Natur.387..783C; 1997MNRAS.288L..51W]
Rapid multi-wavelength follow-up of arcminute localizations, using positional coincidence to chain gamma-ray, X-ray, optical, and radio counterparts [1997Natur.386..686V; 1997Natur.389..261F]
Absorption-line spectroscopy plus Lyman-alpha-forest arguments to bracket afterglow redshifts [1997Natur.387..878M]
Interstellar scintillation analysis to measure afterglow angular sizes and expansion [1997Natur.389..261F]
Discrimination of circumburst density profiles (r^-2 wind vs constant ISM) from afterglow evolution, especially radio [2000ApJ...536..195C]
Statistical tests of angular and brightness distributions (dipole/quadrupole moments, V/Vmax) against galactic source models [1990ApJ...348..485P]
recurring_models: Relativistic fireball with external shock deceleration in ambient medium [1992MNRAS.258P..41R; 1997MNRAS.288L..51W]
Synchrotron emission from shock-accelerated power-law electrons, with adiabatic and fully radiative limiting hydrodynamic evolutions [1998ApJ...497L..17S]
Internal shocks within the ejecta shell for burst variability and precursors; reverse shocks (Newtonian vs relativistic) for duration structure [1995ApJ...455L.143S]
Collimated jet models with lateral spreading, steepening decays and relaxing energy budgets by factors of hundreds [1999ApJ...519L..17S]
Wind interaction models (Wolf-Rayet r^-2 wind) vs constant-density interstellar interaction, mapped to massive-star vs compact-merger progenitors [2000ApJ...536..195C]
Inverse Compton emission dominating early afterglow and explaining delayed GeV photons [1997ApJ...485L...5W]
Cosmological vs galactic-halo source populations as competing distance-scale frameworks [1997Natur.386..686V; 1990ApJ...348..485P]
shaping_results: Prediction that fireball energy is reconverted to radiation on second timescales when Lorentz-factor >~1000 ejecta hit an external medium — the theoretical charter of the field [1992MNRAS.258P..41R]
Prediction of hours-long optical and days-to-weeks radio afterglows decaying as power laws, made before any afterglow was seen [1997ApJ...476..232M; 1993ApJ...418L...5P]
First detection of an X-ray afterglow (GRB 970228), fading as a power law and carrying a significant fraction of the burst energy [1997Natur.387..783C]
First fading optical transient, associated with a faint galaxy and pointing to cosmological distances [1997Natur.386..686V]
First direct distance limit: absorption system at z=0.835 toward GRB 970508, proving at least some bursts are cosmological and highly energetic [1997Natur.387..878M]
First radio afterglow (GRB 970508), with scintillation damping demonstrating source expansion [1997Natur.389..261F]
Month-long power-law afterglow of GRB 970228 matching relativistic blast-wave predictions, implying ~10^51 erg and z~1 [1997MNRAS.288L..51W]
Quantitative confrontation of the fireball model with GRB 970228/970402 data: electron index -2.3±0.1, t^-1 flux decline, xi_e <= 0.6 [1997ApJ...485L...5W]
The standard broken-power-law synchrotron spectrum and light-curve framework with spectral-temporal closure relations [1998ApJ...497L..17S]
Evidence from rapid afterglow decays that GRB outflows are jets, cutting energy requirements by factors of several hundred [1999ApJ...519L..17S]
Internal-shock/deceleration timescale framework linking burst duration and variability to the shell hydrodynamics [1995ApJ...455L.143S]
The BeppoSAX instrument suite whose localizations made the entire afterglow program possible [1991AdSpR..11h.281F]
internal_disagreements: Distance scale (the founding dispute): a countervailing view held that bursts were relatively local objects in a very large galactic halo, against the cosmological interpretation of their isotropic-but-inhomogeneous distribution [1997Natur.386..686V; 1997Natur.387..783C]; galactic neutron-star models were being quantitatively tested and partly ruled out [1990ApJ...348..485P] before the z=0.835 absorption system toward GRB 970508 settled the question in favor of cosmological distances [1997Natur.387..878M]

Circumburst environment: standard afterglow modeling assumed a constant-density external medium [1998ApJ...497L..17S; 1997ApJ...485L...5W], whereas wind-interaction analysis argued GRBs 970228 and 970508 decelerate in a Wolf-Rayet r^-2 wind while 990123 and 990510 favor interstellar interaction — proposing two progenitor types rather than one medium [2000ApJ...536..195C]

Outflow geometry and energetics: spherical blast-wave fits gave total energies of order 10^51 erg [1997MNRAS.288L..51W], but rapid afterglow decays such as GRB 980519's t^-2.05 were argued to be inconsistent with spherical (isotropic) models and to require laterally spreading jets, reducing the energy budget by factors of several hundred [1999ApJ...519L..17S]
Shock hydrodynamics: whether afterglow evolution is fully adiabatic or fully radiative was posed as an open, observationally decidable dichotomy within the synchrotron framework [1998ApJ...497L..17S]
dossiers.activity: Rooted in early-1990s fireball theory [1992MNRAS.258P..41R; 1993ApJ...418L...5P] and instrument building [1991AdSpR..11h.281F], the community ignited in 1997-2000 with the BeppoSAX afterglow discoveries and the model-testing wave that followed [1997Natur.387..783C; 1998ApJ...497L..17S; 2000ApJ...536..195C]. A median year of 2006 across 2136 papers places its peak in the Swift era of routine afterglow follow-up (dark-burst classification work continued through 2004-2011 [2004ApJ...617L..21J; 2011A&A...526A..30G]), with the framework still in active use into the 2010s, e.g. for the X-ray counterpart of GW170817 [2017Natur.551...71T]; the foundational questions are settled and current activity applies the toolkit rather than contesting it.

dossiers.name: Short GRBs and neutron star mergers
dossiers.defining_problem: Establishing that short-duration gamma-ray bursts are produced by the coalescence of compact-object binaries — double neutron stars or neutron star–black hole systems — and working out everything that follows from that identification: the r-process nucleosynthesis and kilonova emission from the merger ejecta [1989Natur.340..126E, 2010MNRAS.406.2650M], the gravitational-wave counterpart [1992ApJ...395L..83N, 2017PhRvL.119p1101A], the host-galaxy demographics that distinguish mergers from massive-star collapse [2005Natur.437..851G, 2005Natur.437..845F], and the nature of the post-merger remnant and its jet [2017ApJ...850L..19M, 2018Natur.561..355M]. The community was founded on theory: Eichler et al. argued in 1989 that coalescing neutron stars should produce gravitational waves, r-process elements, and a subclass of observable gamma-ray bursts simultaneously [1989Natur.340..126E], building on the cosmological-distance hypothesis of Paczynski [1986ApJ...308L..43P, 1991AcA....41..257P]; the identification of the short/hard burst class itself came from BATSE duration bimodality [1993ApJ...413L.101K]. The defining prediction — a gamma-ray burst accompanying a binary-neutron-star gravitational-wave chirp [1992ApJ...395L..83N] — was confirmed 25 years later by GW170817/GRB 170817A, detected 1.7 s after coalescence at 40 Mpc [2017PhRvL.119p1101A, 2017ApJ...848L..12A].
populations_events: Short/hard GRBs (duration < 2 s, harder spectra), identified as a distinct class in the first BATSE catalog [1993ApJ...413L.101K]

GRB 050509B — first rapid arcsecond localization of a short GRB, associated with an elliptical galaxy at z=0.225 in a cluster, 40+/-13 kpc offset, no supernova [2005Natur.437..851G, 2006ApJ...638..354B]
GRB 050709 — first optical afterglow of a short burst, in the outskirts of a star-forming dwarf at z=0.160, supernova definitively excluded [2005Natur.437..845F, 2005Natur.437..859H]
GRB 060614 — a ~102 s burst with no supernova to deep limits but short-like temporal lag and peak luminosity, breaking the two-class scheme [2006Natur.444.1044G]
GRB 130603B — first claimed kilonova, near-infrared excess interpreted as r-process radioactive decay [2013Natur.500..547T]

GW170817 / GRB 170817A / AT 2017gfo — the multi-messenger binary neutron star merger: SNR 32.4 chirp, total mass 2.74 Msun, GRB 1.7 s later, kilonova, and delayed X-ray/radio afterglow [2017PhRvL.119p1101A, 2017ApJ...848L..12A]
The SGR 1806-20 giant flare of 2004, which from a great distance would appear as a short hard GRB [2005Natur.434.1098H]
Double neutron star and NS-BH binaries as gravitational-wave sources for LIGO [1992ApJ...395L..83N, 1992ApJ...400..175B]
instruments_datasets: CGRO/BATSE burst catalogs (duration-hardness classification) [1993ApJ...413L.101K]
Swift BAT/XRT rapid localizations of short bursts [2005Natur.437..851G, 2006ApJ...638..354B]
Advanced LIGO and Advanced Virgo gravitational-wave detectors [2017PhRvL.119p1101A]
Fermi-GBM (detection of GRB 170817A) [2017PhRvL.119p1101A, 2017ApJ...848L..12A]
Ground-based optical/NIR follow-up telescopes and HST for afterglows, hosts, and kilonovae [2005Natur.437..859H, 2013Natur.500..547T]
Radio facilities and VLBI imaging of the GW170817 afterglow [2018Natur.554..207M, 2018Natur.561..355M]
Chandra/XMM X-ray monitoring of GW170817 [2019MNRAS.483.1912P]
characteristic_methods: Duration/hardness distribution analysis for burst classification [1993ApJ...413L.101K]
Rapid multi-wavelength afterglow localization and host-galaxy association by positional coincidence [2005Natur.437..851G, 2006ApJ...638..354B]
Deep optical imaging to include or exclude an accompanying supernova [2005Natur.437..845F, 2006Natur.444.1044G]
Analytic modeling of tidal interaction, mass loss, and fireball formation in inspiraling compact binaries [1992ApJ...400..175B, 1992ApJ...397..570M]
Radioactive-decay light-curve modeling with nuclear reaction networks and radiative transfer (kilonova models) [2010MNRAS.406.2650M]
Gravitational-wave matched-filter detection and parameter estimation [2017PhRvL.119p1101A]
Joint multi-messenger inference combining GW masses with electromagnetic energetics to constrain the remnant and equation of state [2017ApJ...850L..19M]
VLBI proper-motion measurement of merger afterglows [2018Natur.561..355M]
Monte Carlo population synthesis of merger delay-time distributions against redshift samples [2011ApJ...727..109V]
recurring_models: Compact binary coalescence (NS-NS / NS-BH) as the short-GRB central engine, with a post-merger accretion disk or torus [1989Natur.340..126E, 1991AcA....41..257P, 1992ApJ...395L..83N]
The ultrarelativistic e+e- fireball, necessarily anisotropic to escape the neutron-rich ejecta [1986ApJ...308L..43P, 1992ApJ...397..570M, 1992ApJ...395L..83N]

The kilonova: quasi-isotropic transient powered by radioactive decay of r-process nuclei in ~10^-2 Msun of ejecta, with lanthanide opacity pushing emission to the near-infrared [2010MNRAS.406.2650M, 2013Natur.500..547T]
Neutron star mergers as a dominant r-process nucleosynthesis site [1989Natur.340..126E, 2013Natur.500..547T]
The structured/off-axis relativistic jet and its cocoon for GRB 170817A's faint prompt and slowly rising afterglow emission [2018Natur.554..207M, 2018Natur.561..355M]
Magnetar alternatives: extragalactic SGR giant flares for a fraction of short bursts, and long-lived magnetized neutron star remnants [2005Natur.434.1098H, 2019MNRAS.483.1912P]
Two-class (later Type I/Type II) burst taxonomy anchored at the 2 s duration threshold [1993ApJ...413L.101K, 2006Natur.444.1044G, 2011ApJ...727..109V]
shaping_results: Eichler et al. 1989: coalescing neutron stars should jointly produce gravitational-wave bursts, r-process elements, and a subclass of gamma-ray bursts, with consistent rates [1989Natur.340..126E]
Paczynski's cosmological hypothesis: bursts at z~1 requiring ~10^51 erg and relativistic e+e- outflow, with a BH-NS binary decay as the engine [1986ApJ...308L..43P, 1991AcA....41..257P]
Kouveliotou et al. 1993: bimodal BATSE duration distribution splitting GRBs into short/hard and long/soft classes at 2 s [1993ApJ...413L.101K]
Narayan, Paczynski & Piran 1992: merger-powered cosmological fireballs, with the prediction that GRBs are accompanied by LIGO-detectable gravitational radiation [1992ApJ...395L..83N]
Meszaros & Rees 1992: neutron-rich baryonic pollution from tidal mass loss forces merger GRB models to be anisotropic [1992ApJ...397..570M]
Bildsten & Cutler 1992: inspiraling neutron stars cannot be tidally locked, and NS-BH mass transfer is unstable [1992ApJ...400..175B]

The 2005 Swift/HETE-2 breakthrough: GRB 050509B localized to an elliptical galaxy and GRB 050709's optical afterglow with no supernova, ruling out young-population progenitors and favoring coalescing degenerate binaries [2005Natur.437..851G, 2006ApJ...638..354B, 2005Natur.437..845F, 2005Natur.437..859H]
Metzger et al. 2010: quantitative kilonova light curves peaking in ~1 day at ~10^41.5 erg/s for 10^-2 Msun of r-process ejecta [2010MNRAS.406.2650M]
Tanvir et al. 2013: NIR kilonova candidate accompanying GRB 130603B, first direct evidence that mergers make r-process elements [2013Natur.500..547T]

GW170817/GRB 170817A 2017: first direct evidence linking binary neutron star mergers to short GRBs, with the full multi-messenger dataset including kilonova AT 2017gfo [2017PhRvL.119p1101A, 2017ApJ...848L..12A]
Margalit & Metzger 2017: multi-messenger constraint M_max <~ 2.17 Msun on the neutron star maximum mass from GW170817 [2017ApJ...850L..19M]
Mooley et al. 2018: VLBI superluminal motion proving GW170817 launched a successful narrow (<5 deg) relativistic jet viewed ~20 deg off-axis [2018Natur.561..355M]
internal_disagreements: Geometry of the GW170817 outflow: radio light-curve modeling argued there was no signature of an off-axis jet and that a mildly relativistic wide-angle cocoon explained the gamma-ray through radio data [2018Natur.554..207M], whereas subsequent VLBI imaging of superluminal apparent motion broke the choked- vs successful-jet degeneracy and showed the late emission was dominated by an energetic, narrowly collimated (<5 deg) jet [2018Natur.561..355M].

Fate of the GW170817 merger remnant: Margalit & Metzger used the kilonova energetics to argue the remnant collapsed quickly, excluding a long-lived supramassive neutron star and setting M_max <~ 2.17 Msun [2017ApJ...850L..19M], while Piro et al. argued a long-lived magnetized neutron star remnant with GW-dominated spin-down is fully consistent with the electromagnetic dataset, pointing to a ~3-sigma X-ray feature at 155 d as possible central-engine reactivation [2019MNRAS.483.1912P].

Purity of the merger-progenitor hypothesis: the 2005 afterglow discoveries argued young-population models (magnetars, collapsars) are ruled out and coalescing degenerate binaries are the most promising progenitors [2005Natur.437..845F], but Hurley et al. argued from the SGR 1806-20 giant flare that a significant fraction of short GRBs may be extragalactic magnetar flares [2005Natur.434.1098H], and Virgili et al. found that merger models alone cannot reconcile the redshift and flux distributions, requiring either a component tracking star formation or an atypical ~2 Gyr delay [2011ApJ...727..109V].

Validity of the 2 s two-class taxonomy: the BATSE bimodality established short vs long classes at 2 s [1993ApJ...413L.101K], but GRB 060614 — a ~102 s burst with no supernova to deep limits and short-like lag and luminosity — fits neither class, prompting calls for a new classification scheme [2006Natur.444.1044G].
dossiers.activity: Founded by theory papers of 1986-1993 [1986ApJ...308L..43P, 1989Natur.340..126E, 1992ApJ...395L..83N, 1993ApJ...413L.101K], with a first observational surge in 2005-2006 when Swift localized short bursts to their hosts [2005Natur.437..851G, 2006ApJ...638..354B]. The dominant burst of activity follows GW170817 in 2017 — reflected in the community's median year of 2019 and the very heavily cited 2017-2018 multi-messenger papers [2017PhRvL.119p1101A, 2017ApJ...848L..12A, 2018Natur.561..355M]. It remains active into the 2020s on remnant physics, jet structure, and equation-of-state constraints [2019MNRAS.483.1912P], now one of the largest and most current sub-literatures of GRB research (2009 papers).

dossiers.name: GRB Prompt Emission Physics and Polarization
dossiers.defining_problem: What physical mechanism converts the energy of a relativistic GRB outflow into the observed non-thermal gamma-ray spectrum, and what does that mechanism imply about magnetic fields in the ejecta? The community's founding puzzle was the compactness problem — how a source can emit MeV photons without being quenched by pair production [1986ApJ...308L..47G; 1978MNRAS.183..359C]. Its resolution through relativistic fireballs whose radiation is converted to bulk kinetic energy [1990ApJ...365L..55S], rerandomized in external shocks [1993ApJ...405..278M] or internal shocks from an unsteady wind [1994ApJ...430L..93R], set the agenda. Since then the defining question has been whether the prompt emission is synchrotron radiation from shock-accelerated electrons in shock-generated small-scale fields [1994ApJ...432L.107K; 1999ApJ...526..697M], Comptonization in a Poynting-flux-dominated magnetized wind [1994MNRAS.270..480T], or magnetic reconnection in a moderately magnetized jet [2011ApJ...726...90Z] — with gamma-ray and afterglow polarimetry as the decisive observational discriminant [1999ApJ...511..852G; 2003Natur.423..415C; 2019NatAs...3..258Z].

shaping_results: Pair-production opacity sets general constraints on rapidly varying gamma-ray sources and motivates either soft standardized spectra or optically thick, distant, relativistically expanding sources — the compactness problem that founded the field [1978MNRAS.183..359C; 1986ApJ...308L..47G]
Even a small baryon load converts a fireball's radiation into kinetic energy and suppresses the electromagnetic signal, forcing dissipation models [1990ApJ...365L..55S]
External shocks on ambient matter can rerandomize the fireball's bulk kinetic energy into gamma-rays at cosmological distances [1993ApJ...405..278M]
Internal shocks from an unsteady outflow with Gamma ~ 100 dissipate outside the photosphere and convert a substantial fraction of outflow energy to non-thermal radiation [1994ApJ...430L..93R]
BATSE spectra follow the Band form with E_0 peaking below 200 keV and no universal parameter values; a majority are unlikely to be shaped directly by pair processes [1993ApJ...413..281B]
23 of >100 bright BATSE bursts violate the synchrotron alpha <= -2/3 'line of death', challenging the simple synchrotron shock model [1998ApJ...506L..23P]
The relativistic two-stream instability generates skin-depth-scale magnetic fields at 1e-5 to 1e-1 of equipartition in collisionless GRB shocks [1999ApJ...526..697M]
Afterglow polarization up to ~10% is observable if shock-generated field coherence grows near light speed; detection would confirm the synchrotron afterglow model [1999ApJ...511..852G]
A Poynting-flux-dominated MHD wind from a >1e14 G rotator reproduces the broken power-law burst spectrum with essentially no free parameters, without any external medium [1994MNRAS.270..480T]

The claimed near-maximal polarization of GRB 021206 [2003Natur.423..415C] was overturned on re-analysis: the RHESSI signal is consistent with neglected null-lightcurve systematics and carries no polarization constraint [2004MNRAS.350.1288R; 2004ApJ...613.1088W]
The missing bright photosphere in GRB 080916C argued for Poynting-flux-dominated outflows and the ICMART reconnection model [2011ApJ...726...90Z]
The first statistically meaningful polarimeter sample (POLAR, 5 bursts) found polarization lower than popular models predicted, with intrapulse polarization-angle evolution [2019NatAs...3..258Z]
internal_disagreements: The GRB 021206 polarization controversy: Coburn & Boggs claimed the prompt emission was polarized at the theoretical maximum, implying a uniform large-scale magnetic field that drives the explosion [2003Natur.423..415C]; Rutledge & Fox showed the suitable scattering events were overestimated by a factor of ~10 and the signal is consistent with neglected null-lightcurve systematics, yielding no polarization constraint at all [2004MNRAS.350.1288R], and independent RHESSI limits concurred [2004ApJ...613.1088W] — while theorists had already built interpretations on the original claim [2003ApJ...596L..17G; 2003ApJ...597..998L; 2003ApJ...594L..83G]

Synchrotron shock model versus the spectral data: the model predicts a low-energy photon index no harder than -2/3 [1994ApJ...432L.107K], but 23 bright BATSE bursts violate this 'line of death' [1998ApJ...506L..23P], and Band et al. found parameter correlations that do not fulfill cosmological-model predictions and no universal spectral values [1993ApJ...413..281B]; later polarimetric work kept the tension alive with a highly polarized line-of-death violator [2018ApJ...862..154C]

Kinetic-energy-dominated versus Poynting-flux-dominated outflows: the internal-shock picture dissipates bulk kinetic energy of a baryonic wind [1994ApJ...430L..93R; 1993ApJ...405..278M], whereas Thompson's MHD wind generates the spectrum via Comptonization at ~1e10 cm with no external medium at all [1994MNRAS.270..480T], and ICMART argues the missing photosphere of GRB 080916C plus internal-shock efficiency, fast-cooling, and electron-excess problems require a magnetically dominated ejecta dissipating by reconnection [2011ApJ...726...90Z]

Magnetic field structure in the emission region — ordered versus shock-generated random fields: high or variable prompt polarization detections were read as evidence for ordered large-scale fields advected from the central engine [2003ApJ...594L..83G; 2003ApJ...597..998L; 2011ApJ...743L..30Y; 2019ApJ...882L..10S], while the two-stream-instability picture produces small-scale random fields whose net polarization vanishes under circular symmetry [1999ApJ...526..697M]; the POLAR five-burst sample then found polarization at most at a level lower than popular models predicted, attributing earlier claims partly to systematic uncertainties [2019NatAs...3..258Z], even as AstroSat CZTI reported >=3-sigma polarization signatures in 5 of 11 bright bursts [2019ApJ...884..123C]
dossiers.activity: Founded by 1978-1994 theory (compactness, fireballs, internal/external shocks, synchrotron) [1978MNRAS.183..359C; 1986ApJ...308L..47G; 1994ApJ...430L..93R] and BATSE-era spectroscopy [1993ApJ...413..281B]; a second wave in 1998-2004 around the line of death and the GRB 021206 polarization episode [1998ApJ...506L..23P; 2003Natur.423..415C; 2004MNRAS.350.1288R]; the median year of 2013 reflects the peak of the magnetized-jet and polarimetry era (ICMART 2011, GAP/IKAROS 2011, optical polarimetry 2009-2017) [2011ApJ...726...90Z; 2011ApJ...743L..30Y; 2017Natur.547..425T]. Still active: dedicated polarimeter samples (POLAR, AstroSat CZTI) and time-resolved spectroscopy continued through 2019-2025 [2019NatAs...3..258Z; 2022ApJ...936...12C; 2024ApJ...972..132C; 2025ApJ...987..124D].

dossiers.name: GRB multimessenger high-energy astrophysics
dossiers.defining_problem: Whether gamma-ray bursts are the accelerators of the highest-energy particles in the universe — and how to test that with GeV photons, ultra-high-energy cosmic rays, and high-energy neutrinos. The community was seeded by EGRET's detection of GeV photons from bright BATSE bursts, including an 18 GeV photon arriving ~90 minutes after GRB 940217 [1994Natur.372..652H] and a GeV power-law tail from GRB 930131 [1994ApJ...422L..63S; 1994ApJ...422L..59K], and by the theoretical proposals that GRB blast waves naturally produce delayed GeV emission [1994MNRAS.269L..41M] and that GRB internal shocks Fermi-accelerate protons to ~10^20 eV, making GRBs the source of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays [1995PhRvL..75..386W; 1995ApJ...453..883V]. The corollary prediction — that photomeson production in fireballs converts >=10% of the energy into ~10^14 eV neutrinos, detectable at tens of events per year by a km^2 detector [1997PhRvL..78.2292W] — set the agenda that IceCube spent two decades testing [2015ApJ...805L...5A].

shaping_results: EGRET detection of GeV photons from GRB 930131: 16 photons above 30 MeV with photon index -2.0 +/- 0.4, two at ~1 GeV [1994ApJ...422L..63S]

internal_disagreements: Predicted GRB neutrino flux normalization: the founding fireball model predicted a km^2 detector would see at least several tens of events per year [1997PhRvL..78.2292W], but revised numerical calculations with full energy dependencies found the analytical models overestimate the flux by about one order of magnitude [2012PhRvL.108w1101H], and an independent revised analytic calculation likewise obtained a flux one order of magnitude below the IceCube Collaboration's own benchmark [2012ApJ...752...29H] — so whether IceCube's nondetection killed the model or only the early flux arithmetic was disputed

GRBs as UHECR sources: proposed as the origin of cosmic rays above 10^20 eV [1995PhRvL..75..386W; 1995ApJ...453..883V], but photohadronic cascade limits ruled out major GRB contributions above 10^19 eV under standard energetic constraints, finding joint UHECR-plus-neutrino production possible only under extreme conditions [1998PhRvD..58l3005R], and IceCube's stacked limits later disfavored much of the parameter space of the latest UHECR-from-GRB models [2015ApJ...805L...5A]

Origin of delayed GeV photons: leptonic external blast-wave / reverse-shock emission from the decelerating wind [1994MNRAS.269L..41M] versus hadronic pi^0 production by relativistic nucleons striking a dense (~2e11 cm^-3) remnant cloud around the merger [1994ApJ...432L..27K]

Where the observed astrophysical neutrinos come from, given classical GRBs contribute <~1% [2015ApJ...805L...5A]: choked jets and low-luminosity GRBs invisible in gamma rays were advanced as the hidden source population [2013PhRvL.111l1102M; 2016PhRvD..93h3003S]
dossiers.activity: Founded in 1994-1998 by the EGRET GeV detections [1994Natur.372..652H; 1994ApJ...422L..63S] and the UHECR/neutrino predictions [1995PhRvL..75..386W; 1997PhRvL..78.2292W]; most active around the median year 2012, when Fermi-LAT [2009ApJ...697.1071A] and IceCube's deepening nondetections [2012ApJ...752...29H; 2012PhRvL.108w1101H; 2015ApJ...805L...5A] forced model revision. Still alive in the multimessenger era: joint GW170817 neutrino searches in 2017 [2017ApJ...850L..35A], hidden-source models [2016PhRvD..93h3003S], and lepto-hadronic modeling of energetic GRBs as recently as 2023 [2023ApJ...950...28R].

dossiers.name: Collapsar and GRB-supernova connection
dossiers.defining_problem: What stellar systems and central engines produce gamma-ray bursts — specifically, whether long GRBs come from the collapse of massive stars whose cores form a black hole plus hyperaccreting disk ("failed supernova"/collapsar) [1993ApJ...405..273W][1999ApJ...524..262M], and how the burst relates to the accompanying supernova explosion, a question crystallized by the spatial-temporal coincidence of the broad-lined Type Ic SN 1998bw with GRB 980425 [1998Natur.395..670G][1998Natur.395..672I][1998Natur.395..663K]. The community works out the progenitor channels (Wolf-Rayet collapse, helium-star/black-hole mergers, rotating low-metallicity single stars) [1993ApJ...405..273W][1998ApJ...502L...9F][2005A&A...443..643Y], the engine energetics (neutrino annihilation from a thick disk vs. rotating magnetized neutron stars) [1993ApJ...405..273W][1992Natur.357..472U][1996A&A...305..839J], and the observational GRB-SN connection and its exceptions [1998ApJ...504L..87W][2003Natur.423..847H][2006Natur.444.1047F][2022Natur.612..232Y].

Deep photometric supernova/kilonova searches in nearby GRB afterglows to test progenitor predictions [2006Natur.444.1047F, 2022Natur.612..232Y]
recurring_models: The collapsar / failed-supernova model: a rotating Wolf-Rayet or helium core collapses to a black hole plus thick accretion disk that powers a beamed relativistic jet [1993ApJ...405..273W, 1999ApJ...524..262M]
The hypernova: an extremely energetic (~10^52 erg) explosion of a stripped carbon-oxygen star [1998Natur.395..672I, 1998ApJ...494L..45P, 1999ApJ...516..788W]

shaping_results: Woosley's 1993 model showing a black-hole accretion disk from a collapsed rotating Wolf-Rayet star can deposit ~10^50 erg/s via neutrino annihilation, founding the collapsar paradigm [1993ApJ...405..273W]
Discovery of the luminous Type Ic SN 1998bw in the error box of GRB 980425, with gamma-ray energy four orders of magnitude below other GRBs [1998Natur.395..670G]
Light-curve modeling of SN 1998bw requiring ejecta kinetic energy of (2-5)x10^52 erg — the 'hypernova' — implying a new explosion mechanism [1998Natur.395..672I]
Radio observations of SN 1998bw demanding apparent expansion at >=2c, i.e. a relativistic shock from a supernova [1998Natur.395..663K]

MacFadyen & Woosley's 2D collapsar simulations: disk accretion at ~0.07 Msun/s for 10-20 s, jets beamed to ~1% of the sky penetrating the star in ~10 s, predicting collapsars always make SN 1998bw-like supernovae [1999ApJ...524..262M]
Statistical exclusion of Type Ia supernovae as GRB sources (>4 sigma) and consistency of Type Ib/c [1998ApJ...504L..87W]
The argument that GRBs lying in star-forming regions would force abandonment of the neutron-star-merger model for long bursts [1998ApJ...494L..45P]
Spectroscopic confirmation via SN 2003dh/GRB 030329 that long GRBs signal the collapse of massive stars [2003Natur.423..847H]
Discovery of two long GRBs (060505, 060614) with no supernova to limits hundreds of times fainter than SN 1998bw, breaking the universality of the GRB-SN connection [2006Natur.444.1047F]
Yoon & Langer's demonstration that rapidly rotating metal-poor stars evolving chemically homogeneously satisfy collapsar requirements, tying GRB production to low metallicity [2005A&A...443..643Y]
internal_disagreements: White-dwarf collapse as a cosmological GRB source: Usov proposed accretion-induced collapse of magnetized white dwarfs to millisecond magnetars as the cosmological GRB engine [1992Natur.357..472U], while Woosley & Baron computed that the neutrino-driven wind in such a collapse (~0.005 Msun/s mass loss) obscures any prompt display and 'certainly rules out' cosmological GRBs from this channel [1992ApJ...391..228W]

Energetics of neutron-star-merger disks: Woosley 1993 allowed NS mergers as one route to the GRB-powering black-hole disk [1993ApJ...405..273W], but Jaroszynski found that tori from NS-merger parameters give too little energy even with artificially high entropy and viscosity, favoring rotating Wolf-Rayet collapse instead [1996A&A...305..839J]

One GRB class or two: Kulkarni et al. argued SN 1998bw establishes a second class of gamma-ray burst distinctly different from the cosmological kind [1998Natur.395..663K], whereas Woosley, Eastman & Schmidt modeled GRB 980425 as the same black-hole-accretion/jet engine seen with weaker or misaligned jets (Gamma~5 material along the line of sight), i.e. a continuum with ordinary bursts [1999ApJ...516..788W]; Wang & Wheeler went further, taking SN 1998bw-like Ib/c events as possibly the general GRB mechanism with ~10^-3 sr collimation [1998ApJ...504L..87W]

Universality of the GRB-supernova connection: the collapsar simulations predicted that collapsars will always make supernovae similar to SN 1998bw [1999ApJ...524..262M], but GRB 060505 and GRB 060614 showed no supernova to limits hundreds of times fainter than SN 1998bw [2006Natur.444.1047F], and the long-duration GRB 211211A showed kilonova-like emission indicating a non-massive-star (compact-merger) origin, breaking the long-duration = collapsar mapping [2022Natur.612..232Y]

Central engine identity: black-hole hyperaccretion with neutrino annihilation [1993ApJ...405..273W, 1999ApJ...524..262M] versus rapidly rotating, strongly magnetized neutron stars (millisecond magnetars) as the source of the relativistic outflow [1992Natur.357..472U, 1998ApJ...504L..87W]

Progenitor channel: binary routes such as helium-star/black-hole mergers via common-envelope evolution [1998ApJ...502L...9F] versus single rapidly rotating metal-poor stars evolving chemically homogeneously, a channel argued to dominate at low metallicity [2005A&A...443..643Y]
dossiers.activity: Founded in the early 1990s by theory papers on black-hole accretion disks and magnetar formation as cosmological GRB engines [1993ApJ...405..273W, 1992Natur.357..472U, 1992ApJ...391..228W]; exploded in 1998-1999 around SN 1998bw/GRB 980425 and the collapsar simulations [1998Natur.395..670G, 1999ApJ...524..262M]; consolidated in 2003-2007 with the SN 2003dh confirmation and progenitor stellar-evolution work [2003Natur.423..847H, 2005A&A...443..643Y]. With a median year of 2012 for its 1542 papers, the bulk of activity is post-Swift, and the community remains active into the 2020s, now driven by classification-breaking events such as GRB 211211A [2022Natur.612..232Y].

dossiers.name: GRB host galaxies and environments
dossiers.defining_problem: What galaxies and interstellar environments produce gamma-ray bursts, and what that reveals both about the progenitors and about cosmic star formation. The community was founded on the proposition that GRB rates track the cosmic star formation history — first computed for delayed compact-binary mergers against the BATSE brightness distribution [1997ApJ...486L..71T], then inverted by the argument that massive-star remnants make GRBs direct SFR tracers, pushing the dimmest bursts to z~6 [1998MNRAS.294L..13W] and promising a dust-free probe of obscured star formation [2000MNRAS.312L..35B] and of the z>5 universe out to z~10-20 [2000ApJ...536....1L]. Its observational program is host identification and characterization: spectroscopic redshifts, star formation rates, extinctions, and metallicities of the galaxies hosting individual bursts [1998ApJ...508L..17D, 2001ApJ...546..672V], burst-to-host offsets as progenitor diagnostics [2002AJ....123.1111B], and the interpretation of optically dark bursts through dust and gas in the burst environment [1998ApJ...493L..27G, 2000ApJ...537..796W, 2009AJ....138.1690P, 2011A&A...526A..30G]. Its late-phase defining question is whether long GRBs are biased tracers of star formation — specifically whether a host-metallicity threshold governs GRB production [2013ApJ...774..119G, 2015A&A...581A.102V, 2016ApJ...817....8P].

Circumburst radiative processing: dust sublimation out to ~10 pc by the prompt UV flash, time-dependent absorption from ionization of a <~100 pc cloud, H2 absorption/fluorescence in molecular clouds [2000ApJ...537..796W, 1998ApJ...501..467P, 2000ApJ...532..273D]
GRBs as high-redshift probes: absorption spectroscopy of metallicity evolution, Ly-alpha forest, and reionization via the Gunn-Peterson test [2000ApJ...536....1L]
shaping_results: SFR-tracking rate models push the dimmest BATSE bursts to z~6, implying peak luminosities ~20x higher and rates ~150x lower than non-evolving fits — so GRBs are rarer than BNS mergers or beamed [1998MNRAS.294L..13W]

GRB 980703 host: unambiguous z=0.966 and SFR>7 M_sun/yr, early direct evidence tying GRBs to massive star formation [1998ApJ...508L..17D]
Median burst-host offset of 1.3 kpc tracking host UV light; delayed merging remnants ruled out at the 2x10^-3 level for long GRBs [2002AJ....123.1111B]
Prediction of the host population from SFR-tracking models: hosts peak at z~1, I=21.5-28, ~15% at z>2.5 like Lyman-break galaxies [1998A&A...339L...1M]
GRB hosts are sub-luminous, blue, low-mass galaxies, hinting at a metal-poor preference consistent with collapsars [2003A&A...400..499L]

SHOALS: GRB production is suppressed only above ~solar metallicity, a threshold high enough to favor binary progenitors [2016ApJ...817....8P]
GRBs established as probes of z>5: detectable to z~10-20, tracing metallicity evolution and reionization [2000ApJ...536....1L]
Dust sublimation by the prompt flash reconciles unreddened afterglows with star-forming-region birthplaces [2000ApJ...537..796W]
internal_disagreements: Progenitor identity read from hosts: the community founder computed GRB rates assuming delayed binary neutron star mergers [1997ApJ...486L..71T], while the offset distribution of 20 long GRBs later ruled out delayed merging remnants at the 2x10^-3 level in favor of collapsar-like progenitors tracing host UV light [2002AJ....123.1111B]; already in 1998 the SFR-tracking flux fits implied GRBs are far rarer than BNS mergers unless strongly beamed [1998MNRAS.294L..13W].

How strong is the metallicity bias: Graham & Fruchter find three quarters of long-GRB hosts below 12+log(O/H)=8.6 and call sub-half-solar metallicity a fundamental requirement [2013ApJ...774..119G]; the BAT6 sample requires a threshold of 0.3-0.5 Z_sun and excludes both no-threshold and extreme 0.1 Z_sun models [2015A&A...581A.102V]; SHOALS instead places the suppression threshold near solar metallicity — much higher, and favoring binary progenitors over single-star models [2016ApJ...817....8P]; while GRB 020819's host environment at 12+log(O/H)=9.0 stands as a direct high-metallicity counterexample [2010ApJ...712L..26L].

Are GRBs unbiased SFR tracers at all: the founding program treated the burst redshift distribution as a dust-free tracer of massive star formation [2000MNRAS.312L..35B, 1998MNRAS.294L..13W], but the BAT6 host analysis concludes long GRBs are not unbiased tracers at z<1 and only track SFR directly from z~4 [2015A&A...581A.102V]; SHOALS confines the bias to z<1.5 with minor impact at higher redshift [2016ApJ...817....8P].

What makes dark bursts dark: H2 absorption in molecular clouds was proposed to explain the GRB 980329 cutoff at inferred 3.0<z<4.4 without dust [2000ApJ...532..273D], and dust sublimation by the prompt flash was argued to clear dust so that unreddened fireballs stay consistent with star-forming regions [2000ApJ...537..796W]; the Swift-era resolution attributes darkness dominantly to dust extinction local to the progenitor [2009AJ....138.1690P], with GROND quantifying moderate intrinsic extinction plus a ~22% z>5 tail [2011A&A...526A..30G].
dossiers.activity: Founded 1997-2000 in the afterglow era (Totani 1997, Wijers 1998, the first host spectroscopy in 1998 [1998ApJ...508L..17D]), with a first observational consolidation in 2001-2003 (offsets [2002AJ....123.1111B], host demographics [2003A&A...400..499L]). Peak activity in the Swift era, consistent with the community median year of 2012: the dark-burst census (2009-2011 [2009AJ....138.1690P, 2011A&A...526A..30G]) and the complete-sample host surveys TOUGH 2012 [2012ApJ...756..187H], BAT6 2015-2019 [2015A&A...581A.102V, 2019A&A...623A..26P], and SHOALS 2016 [2016ApJ...817....8P]. Currently mature and tapering: the big statistical questions (metallicity threshold, tracer bias) were largely framed and bounded by 2016-2019, and the corpus shows its host-identification toolkit being inherited by fast-radio-burst host studies from 2016 onward [2017ApJ...834L...7T].

dossiers.name: GRB Luminosity Correlations and Cosmology
dossiers.defining_problem: Whether empirical correlations between prompt-emission observables of gamma-ray bursts and their intrinsic luminosity or energy can turn GRBs into standardizable candles — first to assign distances to bursts without redshifts, then to extend the Hubble diagram beyond the supernova range and constrain dark energy. The founding move was the discovery that spectral lag anticorrelates with peak luminosity, L_53 ~ 1.3(tau/0.01 s)^-1.15 [2000ApJ...534..248N], paralleled by the luminosity-variability correlation [2001ApJ...552...57R] and the E_peak-E_iso (Amati) correlation found in twelve BeppoSAX bursts with redshifts [2002A&A...390...81A]. The community's defining tension is whether these relations are intrinsic physics or artifacts of detector thresholds and redshift-measurement selection [2005ApJ...627..319B, 2007ApJ...671..656B, 2013A&A...557A.100H].

shaping_results: The lag-luminosity anticorrelation L_53 ~ 1.3(tau/0.01 s)^-1.15 in bursts with redshifts, founding the luminosity-indicator program [2000ApJ...534..248N]

The Ghirlanda relation: collimation-corrected E_gamma correlates tightly with E_peak, E_peak(1+z) ~ E_gamma^0.7, immediately proposed for cosmology [2004ApJ...616..331G]

The 69-burst GRB Hubble diagram to z>6 combining five luminosity indicators, finding concordance LambdaCDM consistent at rms scatter 0.65 mag, only a factor 2 worse than supernova surveys [2007ApJ...660...16S]

The counterattack: 88% of BATSE bursts are inconsistent with the Amati relation, implying it is a selection artifact [2005ApJ...627..319B], and the Swift catalog showing pre-Swift correlations inconsistent at >5 sigma and partially correlated with detector threshold [2007ApJ...671..656B]
The k-correction methodology showing uncorrected energies undercount bolometric output by 5-600%, standardizing all subsequent energetics work [2001AJ....121.2879B]
internal_disagreements: Intrinsic physics vs selection artifact — the community's central war. Amati et al. reported the E_p-E_iso correlation while acknowledging possible truncation biases [2002A&A...390...81A], and Lloyd et al. argued the E_p-fluence correlation must be intrinsic [2000ApJ...534..227L]; Band & Preece countered that 88% of BATSE bursts violate the Amati relation and about a third violate the Ghirlanda relation, making them sample artifacts [2005ApJ...627..319B]; Butler et al. found the Swift correlation inconsistent with the pre-Swift one at >5 sigma and arising artificially from the detector threshold [2007ApJ...671..656B]; Heussaff et al. attempted a synthesis with Fermi data: a real physical lower-right boundary in the E_p-E_iso plane plus redshift-measurement selection producing the apparent tightness [2013A&A...557A.100H].

Whether GRBs may be used for cosmology at all: Dai et al. derived Omega_M and w from the Ghirlanda relation [2004ApJ...612L.101D] and Schaefer built a 69-burst Hubble diagram concluding the concordance model fits [2007ApJ...660...16S], while Butler et al. declared the pre-Swift correlations 'likely useless for tests of cosmology' [2007ApJ...671..656B] and Collazzi et al. concluded the Amati relation 'should not be used for cosmological purposes' — while explicitly exempting the other luminosity relations [2012ApJ...747...39C].

The status of GRB 980425/SN 1998bw: it falls below the lag-luminosity relation by a factor of several hundred [2000ApJ...534..248N], but its luminosity and variability are consistent with the L-V fit, suggesting a common origin with cosmological bursts [2001ApJ...552...57R], and viewing-angle jet kinematics can reproduce the lag-luminosity relation including 980425 as a large-viewing-angle event [2001ApJ...554L.163I].

Redshift evolution of the relations: Yonetoku et al. assumed a universal E_p-luminosity relation to derive pseudo-redshifts [2004ApJ...609..935Y], whereas Li found the Amati parameters vary systematically with redshift with only ~4% probability of being a fluence-limit selection effect, implying strong evolution that would bias any uncorrected cosmological use [2007MNRAS.379L..55L].

GRB rate vs star formation rate: the E_p-luminosity pseudo-redshift analysis found the GRB rate well correlated with the SFR at z<=2 [2004ApJ...609..935Y], while the earlier fluence-based nonparametric study found a GRB comoving rate density quite different from the star formation rate [1999ApJ...511..550L].
dossiers.activity: Founded 1999-2002 with the lag-luminosity, variability, and Amati relations [2000ApJ...534..248N, 2001ApJ...552...57R, 2002A&A...390...81A]; peak construction phase 2004-2007 when the Ghirlanda and Yonetoku relations were converted into dark-energy constraints and Hubble diagrams [2004ApJ...616..331G, 2004ApJ...612L.101D, 2004ApJ...609..935Y, 2007ApJ...660...16S], immediately shadowed by the selection-effects counterattack [2005ApJ...627..319B, 2007ApJ...671..656B]. The median year of 2013 reflects the long adjudication phase with Swift and Fermi samples [2012ApJ...747...39C, 2013A&A...557A.100H]; the field remains active in cosmology-tension work, e.g. GRB-augmented high-redshift Hubble diagrams testing flat LambdaCDM [2019A&A...628L...4L], but the correlation-discovery era is over.

dossiers.name: GRB Lorentz Invariance Violation Tests
dossiers.defining_problem: Whether quantum gravity leaves an observable imprint on photon propagation over cosmological distances — specifically an energy-dependent speed of light (vacuum dispersion) or vacuum birefringence suppressed by the Planck scale — and whether gamma-ray bursts, by combining GeV–TeV photon energies, millisecond variability, and known redshifts, can push time-of-flight and polarization constraints to and beyond E_Planck ~ 1.22e19 GeV. The program was founded by the proposal that GRB arrival-time differences across energy bands are sensitive to Planck-scale dispersion [1998Natur.393..763A], theoretically grounded in loop-quantum-gravity predictions of nonstandard vacuum optics [1999PhRvD..59l4021G], and its persistent core difficulty is the degeneracy between propagation-induced delays and intrinsic source spectral lags [2006APh....25..402E, 2000ApJ...535..139E, 2004ApJ...611L..77B].
