Gambini & Pullin derived helicity-dependent corrections to Maxwell's equations from loop quantum gravity, giving the program a concrete theoretical target [1999PhRvD..59l4021G]
Schaefer set early severe limits: Delta-c/c < 6.3e-21, m_gamma < 4.2e-44 g, E_QG > 8.3e16 GeV from BATSE GRB flares [1999PhRvL..82.4964S]

Ellis et al. introduced the redshift-regression method on BATSE/OSSE GRBs, obtaining M > ~1e15 GeV [2000ApJ...535..139E], refined with wavelet timing to M >= 6.9e15 GeV [2003A&A...402..409E], and then to a robust M > 0.9e16 GeV while finding a systematic tendency for energetic photons to arrive earlier that is degenerate with intrinsic lags [2006APh....25..402E]

Jacobson, Liberati & Mattingly used the (since-disputed) GRB 021206 polarization plus Crab vacuum-Cherenkov arguments to improve EFT Lorentz-violation bounds by 10 orders of magnitude [2004PhRvL..93b1101J]
MAGIC found a 2.5-sigma energy-dependent delay in a Mkn 501 flare, the community's most discussed positive hint outside GRBs [2008PhLB..668..253M]
Fermi-LAT's GRB 090510 gave the watershed single-event limit M > 1.2 E_Planck for linear dispersion, disfavoring linear quantum-gravity models [2009Natur.462..331A]
LHAASO TeV photons from GRB 221009A pushed limits to >5.9 E_Planck (linear) and the best quadratic time-of-flight limits [2024PhRvD.109h1501P]
internal_disagreements: Positive light-speed-variation claims vs Planck-scale null limits: Zhang & Ma report that Fermi-LAT Pass 8 bright-GRB events support an energy-dependent light speed with linear and quadratic corrections [2015APh....61..108Z], Xu & Ma find evidence for a linear light-speed modification from GRB 160509A [2016PhLB..760..602X], and Zhu & Ma argue the 99.3 GeV photon of GRB 221009A is consistent with E_LV = 3.6e17 GeV [2023JPhG...50fLT01Z]. This is directly contradicted by the GRB 090510 limit M > 1.2 E_Planck ~ 1.5e19 GeV [2009Natur.462..331A] and by LHAASO GRB 221009A limits > 5.9 E_Planck [2024PhRvD.109h1501P], which explicitly confirm stringent limits from other GRBs; Ganguly & Desai likewise conclude the GRB 160625B spectral-lag transition, even if real, cannot be LIV because it would violate prior limits by 3-4 orders of magnitude and must be intrinsic [2017APh....94...17G].

The GRB 021206 polarization retraction: Coburn & Boggs claimed near-maximal (80±20%) linear polarization of the prompt emission from RHESSI data [2003Natur.423..415C], and this measurement underpinned the 1e10-fold improvement in birefringence LIV bounds [2004PhRvL..93b1101J] and Lorentz-invariance tests on the same burst [2004ApJ...611L..77B]; Rutledge & Fox re-analyzed the RHESSI data and found the burst was not 80±20% polarized, that Coburn & Boggs overestimated usable scattering events by a factor of 10, and that the signal-to-noise could not yield a detection even for a 100% polarized source [2004MNRAS.350.1288R].

Propagation effect vs intrinsic source lags: Ellis et al. found a systematic tendency for more energetic photons to arrive earlier across a large GRB sample, but showed the intrinsic-lag and propagation parameters are strongly degenerate and the significance weakens for robust features, so they published only a lower limit [2006APh....25..402E]; the MAGIC collaboration similarly could not exclude a source effect behind their 2.5-sigma Mkn 501 delay [2008PhLB..668..253M], while the Ma-group papers attribute equivalent time lags to genuine propagation effects [2016PhLB..760..602X, 2023JPhG...50fLT01Z].
dossiers.activity: Founded 1998-2000 by the Amelino-Camelia proposal and loop-quantum-gravity phenomenology [1998Natur.393..763A, 1999PhRvD..59l4021G, 2000PhRvL..84.2318A]; a BATSE-era constraint wave 1999-2006 [1999PhRvL..82.4964S, 2000ApJ...535..139E, 2003A&A...402..409E, 2006APh....25..402E]; reinvigorated by MAGIC and Fermi 2008-2009 [2008PhLB..668..253M, 2009Natur.462..331A]. The median year of 2017 reflects its most active recent phase, the 2015-2018 Ma-group light-speed-variation claims and their rebuttals [2015APh....61..108Z, 2016PhLB..760..602X, 2017APh....94...17G]. It remains active: GRB 221009A/LHAASO produced both a new positive claim [2023JPhG...50fLT01Z] and the strongest-ever time-of-flight limits [2024PhRvD.109h1501P].

dossiers.name: GRB Monitors and Terrestrial Gamma-ray Flashes
dossiers.defining_problem: This community sits at the instrumental heart of GRB astronomy rather than its astrophysics: it is the literature of wide-field gamma-ray burst monitors as instruments — their localization accuracy, calibration, and detector design — together with the atmospheric-physics science those same monitors do as a byproduct, above all terrestrial gamma-ray flashes (TGFs). The founder paper quantified Fermi-GBM localization systematics, showing statistical uncertainties as small as 1 degree hide a 3.7-degree systematic Gaussian with a ~14-degree tail [2015ApJS..216...32C]. The parallel defining thread asks what produces millisecond-scale MeV flashes from thunderstorms: whether TGFs are directly tied to lightning discharges [1996GeoRL..23.1017I; 2010JGRA..11512307C], what electron-acceleration mechanism (large-scale relativistic runaway avalanche versus lightning-leader fields) generates them [2016JGRA..12111346M; 2019JGRA..124.7170M], and how a new generation of monitors (GECAM, Insight-HXMT, HERMES, GRID) can localize both cosmic GRBs and gravitational-wave counterparts [2019NIMPA.921....8Z; 2020SCPMA..6349503L; 2019NIMPA.936..199F; 2019ExA....48...77W].
populations_events: Terrestrial gamma-ray flashes: 12 in Fermi-GBM's first year [2010JGRA..115.7323B], 384 with improved analysis [2013JGRA..118.3805B], 4,144 in the first GBM TGF catalog at ~800/yr [2018JGRA..123.4381R], 217 seen by ASIM in 10 months [2019JGRD..12414024O], with an inferred global rate of ~400,000/yr [2013JGRA..118.3805B]
BATSE terrestrial gamma flashes: 13 events with ~50 microsecond variability, spectrally harder than cosmic GRBs [1997JGR...102.9659N]
Terrestrial electron beams: >1 ms GBM events from electrons traveling along geomagnetic field lines, carrying 511 keV positron-annihilation signatures [2011GeoRL..38.2808B]
Ground-level thundercloud gamma-ray bursts with associated photonuclear neutrons, observed at coastal Japan [2016PhLB..758..286K]
The 300+ independently localized GRBs used to calibrate GBM systematics out of >1400 GBM detections [2015ApJS..216...32C]
Accreting pulsars monitored by GBM/BAT, e.g. the 2008 torque reversal of 4U 1626-67 [2010ApJ...708.1500C]
Anticipated GW-GRB coincidences: a few per year at a 200 Mpc horizon for CubeSat constellations [2019ExA....48...77W]
instruments_datasets: Fermi Gamma-ray Burst Monitor (GBM) — the community's central instrument for GRB localization and TGF detection [2015ApJS..216...32C; 2010JGRA..115.7323B; 2018JGRA..123.4381R]
CGRO/BATSE — the founding TGF and GRB-monitor dataset [1997JGR...102.9659N]
World Wide Lightning Location Network (WWLLN) sferic data for TGF-lightning association [2010JGRA..11512307C; 2018JGRA..123.4381R]
ELF/VLF radio atmospherics receivers (Palmer Station) and broadband 1-300 kHz magnetic-field measurements [1996GeoRL..23.1017I; 2011GeoRL..3814810C]
GECAM twin satellites with LaBr3:Ce + SiPM gamma-ray detectors, 6 keV-5 MeV [2019NIMPA.921....8Z]
Insight-HXMT High Energy telescope: 18 NaI/CsI phoswich detectors, ~5100 cm^2, 20-250 keV plus 0.2-3 MeV GRB monitoring [2020SCPMA..6349503L]
HERMES nano-satellite constellation (GAGG:Ce + SDD detectors) [2019NIMPA.936..199F]
GRID student CubeSat network, 10 keV-2 MeV [2019ExA....48...77W]
MAXI all-sky X-ray monitor on the ISS, 0.5-30 keV [2009PASJ...61..999M]
ASIM Modular X- and Gamma-ray Sensor on the ISS [2019JGRD..12414024O]
Swift/BAT long-term hard X-ray monitoring [2010ApJ...708.1500C]
PANDA 360 kg plastic-scintillator prototype for ground-level TGF detection [2016PhLB..758..286K]
characteristic_methods: Cross-validation of monitor localizations against independently localized GRBs (Swift, LAT, INTEGRAL, MAXI, IPN) with Gaussian modeling of systematic error distributions [2015ApJS..216...32C]
Microsecond-accuracy temporal cross-correlation of satellite gamma-ray data with radio sferics from lightning networks [2010JGRA..11512307C; 2011GeoRL..3814810C; 1996GeoRL..23.1017I]

Individual-TGF spectral fitting with Poisson likelihood against Monte Carlo RREA and lightning-leader templates, inferring source altitude from atmospheric absorption [2016JGRA..12111346M; 2019JGRA..124.7170M]
Offline search algorithms, new data modes, and cosmic-ray-shower rejection to expand TGF samples tenfold [2013JGRA..118.3805B]
Bayesian-block temporal/spectral characterization of catalog-scale TGF samples [2018JGRA..123.4381R]
Light-travel-time arguments constraining source size from pulse risetimes [2010JGRA..115.7323B]
Detector design, ground calibration with radioactive sources, and Geant4 background simulation for new monitors [2019NIMPA.921....8Z; 2020SCPMA..6349503L]
Triangulation and flux-modulation localization across satellite constellations [2019NIMPA.936..199F; 2019ExA....48...77W]
Long-term pulse timing and hardness-ratio monitoring of accreting pulsars with GBM/BAT [2010ApJ...708.1500C]
recurring_models: Relativistic runaway electron avalanche (RREA) in large-scale organized thundercloud electric fields as the TGF acceleration mechanism [2016JGRA..12111346M; 2016PhLB..758..286K]
Lightning-leader-tip field acceleration (high- and low-potential leader models, often with tilted beams) as the competing TGF mechanism [2019JGRA..124.7170M]
Bremsstrahlung from runaway electrons plus atmospheric photon propagation as the spectral forward model, making source altitude a fitted parameter [2016JGRA..12111346M; 2019JGRA..124.7170M]
Geomagnetic-field-line transport of electron-positron beams from TGF sources to spacecraft (electron TGFs) [2011GeoRL..38.2808B; 2010JGRA..11512307C]
Gaussian-core-plus-tail systematic error models for monitor localizations [2015ApJS..216...32C]
Constellation triangulation with sub-microsecond timing as the localization paradigm for next-generation monitors [2019NIMPA.936..199F; 2019ExA....48...77W]
shaping_results: The first direct association of a terrestrial gamma-ray burst with a lightning discharge, via a sferic within +/-1.5 ms [1996GeoRL..23.1017I]
BATSE TGFs vary on ~50 microsecond timescales and are spectrally much harder than cosmic GRBs, establishing them as a distinct phenomenon [1997JGR...102.9659N]
Fermi-GBM's first TGFs: ~30 MeV maximum energies, 7 microsecond risetimes constraining source radii to <2 km [2010JGRA..115.7323B]
13 of 15 GBM TGF-WWLLN associations simultaneous to ~40 microseconds, tying TGFs directly to lightning discharges [2010JGRA..11512307C]
Discovery of 511 keV annihilation lines in electron TGFs: lightning produces electron-positron pair beams injected into the near-Earth environment [2011GeoRL..38.2808B]
New GBM data modes raised the TGF detection rate tenfold and implied ~400,000 TGFs globally per year [2013JGRA..118.3805B]
The first Fermi-GBM TGF catalog: 4,144 events, with hard photons lagging soft by ~27 microseconds [2018JGRA..123.4381R]
GBM GRB localizations carry a 3.7-degree systematic uncertainty with a ~14-degree non-Gaussian tail — the number that drove the push for better-localizing monitors [2015ApJS..216...32C]
MAXI established ISS-based all-sky X-ray monitoring down to ~2 mCrab per week [2009PASJ...61..999M]
GECAM's LaBr3:Ce/SiPM detector achieved 5.3% resolution at 662 keV over 6 keV-5 MeV, defining the post-GBM monitor design [2019NIMPA.921....8Z]
Insight-HXMT/HE demonstrated a ~5100 cm^2 phoswich telescope doubling as a 0.2-3 MeV GRB monitor [2020SCPMA..6349503L]
GBM/BAT long-term monitoring caught the second torque reversal of 4U 1626-67, showing GRB monitors' value for accreting-pulsar timing [2010ApJ...708.1500C]
internal_disagreements: TGF-lightning temporal ordering: the first GBM TGF paper reported an inconsistent sequence — one TGF before its lightning stroke, two simultaneous, one after [2010JGRA..115.7323B] — whereas the WWLLN association study found 13 of 15 associations simultaneous to ~40 microseconds and argued a large fraction of TGFs are coincident with the discharge [2010JGRA..11512307C]; microsecond magnetic-field work then split the difference, finding fast discharge-like processes with no consistent timing relationship but a slower radio component that mirrors the gamma-ray profile [2011GeoRL..3814810C]

TGF production mechanism: individual-TGF spectroscopy concluded that narrow-beam events require large-scale RREA in organized electric fields and appear inconsistent with lightning-leader acceleration models [2016JGRA..12111346M], while a subsequent leader-model analysis of 66 bright GBM TGFs found 59% best fit by high-potential leader models and concluded spectral analysis alone cannot strongly discriminate between the mechanisms [2019JGRA..124.7170M]

TGF source altitude and the sprite connection: the founding papers speculated TGFs were tied to high-altitude phenomena, with slow-tail sferics resembling sprite-associated discharges [1996GeoRL..23.1017I] and BATSE timing argued to favor a red-sprite over blue-jet relation [1997JGR...102.9659N]; later spectral fits placed TGF sources inside thunderclouds at 11.6-20.2 km [2016JGRA..12111346M] and mostly below 15 km [2019JGRA..124.7170M], displacing the sprite-altitude picture
dossiers.activity: Founded in the BATSE era (1996-1997) with the TGF-lightning association papers [1996GeoRL..23.1017I; 1997JGR...102.9659N], the community's first boom came with Fermi-GBM TGF science in 2010-2013 [2010JGRA..115.7323B; 2013JGRA..118.3805B], matured into catalogs by 2018-2019 [2018JGRA..123.4381R; 2019JGRD..12414024O], and then pivoted toward next-generation monitor instrumentation (GECAM, HXMT, HERMES, GRID) in 2019-2022 [2019NIMPA.921....8Z; 2020SCPMA..6349503L; 2019NIMPA.936..199F; 2019ExA....48...77W]. With a median year of 2021, it is currently active, dominated by the instrument-paper wave for GW-counterpart monitors rather than by new TGF physics.

dossiers.name: Fireshell / binary-driven hypernova program
dossiers.defining_problem: To explain the entire GRB phenomenon — energetics, light-curve structure, spectra, the GRB-supernova connection, and burst classification — from first-principles relativistic field theory and binary stellar evolution, rather than from the standard fireball/internal-shock framework. The founding problem is whether vacuum polarization around a charged ("electromagnetic") black hole can power GRBs: the dyadosphere, the region where the field exceeds the Heisenberg-Euler critical value for e+e- pair creation, was proposed as the GRB energy source [1998A&A...338L..87P], with the resulting pair-electromagnetic (PEM) pulse computed via general-relativistic hydrodynamics to yield Lorentz factors up to 6x10^3 and photon energies of 10^52-10^54 erg consistent with observed bursts [1999A&A...350..334R, 1999A&AS..138..511R]. The later phase of the problem became the progenitor question: how a tight CO-core + neutron-star binary produces a GRB when the supernova of the core drives hypercritical accretion onto the companion NS, collapsing it to a black hole — the induced-gravitational-collapse / binary-driven-hypernova (BdHN) paradigm [2012ApJ...758L...7R, 2014ApJ...793L..36F].
populations_events: GRB 991216 — the community's original prototype, used to fix the two free parameters of the EMBH model and to define the injector/beam-target burst-structure paradigm [2001ApJ...555L.113R, 2001ApJ...555L.107R, 2002ApJ...581L..19R], and whose Chandra iron lines motivated the induced-supernova scenario [2001ApJ...555L.117R]
GRB 130427A / SN 2013cq — prototype Type I BdHN, used to calibrate the Kerr-BH 'inner engine' for GeV emission (M = 2.31 M_sun, spin 0.47, B0 = 3.5x10^10 G) [2019ApJ...886...82R]
GRB 090510 — the community's flagship short burst, analyzed twice with contradictory classifications [2013ApJ...772...62M, 2016ApJ...831..178R]
GRB 060614 — interpreted as a 'disguised' short GRB from an old merging binary in a galactic halo (CBM density ~10^-3 cm^-3), explaining the absent supernova [2009A&A...498..501C]
GRB 090618 — two-episode burst read as a 'proto-black hole' precursor plus a genuine long GRB [2012A&A...543A..10I]
GRB 090227B — claimed 'missing link' between genuine short and long GRBs [2013ApJ...763..125M]
The community's own GRB taxonomy: XRFs vs BdHNe among long bursts and S-GRFs vs genuine S-GRBs among short bursts, split at E_iso = 10^52 erg by whether a black hole forms [2016ApJ...832..136R]
BATSE duration/hardness subpopulations and their brightness distributions, an early statistical strand [1998ApJ...497L..21T]
instruments_datasets: BATSE (burst catalogs, brightness/hardness distributions, GRB 991216 light curves) [1998ApJ...497L..21T, 2001ApJ...555L.113R]
Rossi X-Ray Timing Explorer and Chandra (GRB 991216 afterglow and iron emission lines) [2001ApJ...555L.113R, 2001ApJ...555L.117R]
Swift BAT/XRT (light-curve fitting of GRB 060614; the flare-plateau-afterglow sample of BdHNe) [2009A&A...498..501C, 2018ApJ...852...53R]
Fermi (GBM/LAT) and AGILE for GRB 090510 and the GeV emission of GRB 130427A [2013ApJ...772...62M, 2019ApJ...886...82R]
Multi-satellite joint spectroscopy — Fermi, Swift, Konus-WIND, AGILE, RT-2, Suzaku — for GRB 090618 [2012A&A...543A..10I]
characteristic_methods: General-relativistic and special-relativistic hydrodynamic integration of expanding e+e- pair plasmas, with the validated constant-thickness slab approximation [1999A&A...350..334R, 2000A&A...359..855R, 1999A&AS..138..511R]
Two-parameter fireshell fitting: total e+e- plasma energy plus baryon load B, with the circumburst-medium density profile reconstructed from the light curve [2009A&A...498..501C, 2013ApJ...772...62M]

Identification of the P-GRB (transparency emission) versus 'extended afterglow' in prompt light curves, and paradigm-based reinterpretation of burst structure [2001ApJ...555L.113R, 2012A&A...543A..10I]
Exact equitemporal-surface computation from Taub's relativistic hydrodynamics, contrasted with the approximate EQTS of Panaitescu & Meszaros, Sari, and Granot [2004ApJ...605L...1B]
Analytical Bondi-Hoyle hypercritical-accretion calculations and full numerical/SPH simulations of SN ejecta accreting onto a NS companion [2012ApJ...758L...7R, 2014ApJ...793L..36F]
Kerr black-hole electrodynamics in a uniform aligned magnetic field ('inner engine') with synchrotron modeling of the GeV component [2019ApJ...886...82R]
Statistical brightness-distribution (Euclidean vs non-Euclidean) tests on BATSE duration/hardness subclasses [1998ApJ...497L..21T]
recurring_models: Dyadosphere / electromagnetic black hole (EMBH): vacuum polarization above the Heisenberg-Euler critical field around a Reissner-Nordstrom BH as the GRB energy source [1998A&A...338L..87P, 1999A&A...350..334R]

PEM pulse / fireshell: an optically thick e+e--photon plasma shell that accelerates, engulfs a baryonic remnant, and emits the P-GRB at transparency, followed by 'extended afterglow' from CBM collisions [2000A&A...359..855R, 2001A&A...368..377B, 2009A&A...498..501C]
The interpretation-of-burst-structure and relative-spacetime-transformation paradigms (injector phase vs beam-target phase; four time variables) [2001ApJ...555L.113R, 2001ApJ...555L.107R]

Induced gravitational collapse / binary-driven hypernova: SN of a CO core drives hypercritical accretion onto a NS companion that collapses to a BH in ~10^2-10^3 s, emitting the GRB [2012ApJ...758L...7R, 2014ApJ...793L..36F]
The seven-subclass BdHN taxonomy with the E_iso = 10^52 erg black-hole-formation threshold and GeV emission as the BH discriminant [2016ApJ...832..136R, 2016ApJ...831..178R]
'Disguised' short GRBs: long-duration events from old compact binaries in low-density halo environments [2009A&A...498..501C, 2010-era companions]
The Kerr-BH 'inner engine' operating in elementary ~10^37 erg impulses to produce GeV/TeV emission and UHECRs [2019ApJ...886...82R]
shaping_results: Definition of the dyadosphere and the demonstration that its pair-creation energetics can meet GRB energy requirements, including GRB 971214 at z=3.4 [1998A&A...338L..87P]

Validation of the constant-thickness PEM-pulse model against full GR hydrodynamics, yielding Lorentz factors up to 6x10^3 and photon energies 10^52-10^54 erg from EMBH parameters alone [1999A&A...350..334R, 2000A&A...359..855R]

The GRB 991216 trilogy fixing the model's two free parameters from the afterglow and recasting the 'prompt emission' as afterglow-peak substructure from ISM inhomogeneities at gamma ~ 310, declaring the external-shock model the winner over internal shocks [2001ApJ...555L.113R, 2002ApJ...581L..19R]
The FRED-shaped elementary spike computed from a pure e+e- PEM pulse without fitting [2001A&A...368..377B]
Exact equitemporal surfaces differing from the standard approximate ones used in afterglow modeling [2004ApJ...605L...1B]

The IGC result that a NS companion accreting Type Ib/c SN ejecta reaches critical mass in seconds and collapses to a BH, explaining GRB-SN temporal coincidence and the exclusive association with helium-poor SNe Ic [2012ApJ...758L...7R, 2014ApJ...793L..36F]
The four/seven-subclass classification of GRBs with the 10^52 erg BH-formation threshold [2016ApJ...832..136R]
X-ray flares in BdHNe shown to be thermal emission at ~10^12 cm with Gamma <= 4, argued to be incompatible with a single ultrarelativistic fireball jet [2018ApJ...852...53R]
The self-consistent Kerr-BH inner-engine parameters for GRB 130427A (M = 2.31 M_sun, alpha = 0.47, B0 = 3.48x10^10 G) as the origin of its GeV emission [2019ApJ...886...82R]
internal_disagreements: GRB 090510 was classified in two mutually exclusive ways within the same framework: first as a 'disguised short GRB by excess' — an event in an overdense medium (n_CBM ~ 1.85x10^3 cm^-3) defining a new burst family [2013ApJ...772...62M] — and three years later as a 'genuine short GRB' (S-GRB) from a binary neutron star coalescing into a Kerr-Newman black hole, with GeV emission as the BH-formation discriminant [2016ApJ...831..178R]. The two papers assign the same event to different progenitors and different environment classes.

The direction of causation in the GRB-supernova connection was reversed within the community. The 2001 induced-supernova paradigm had the GRB come first: the progenitor P1 collapses to an EMBH and its burst impacts a nearby companion star P2, inducing the supernova whose remnant produces the iron lines 18.5 hr later [2001ApJ...555L.117R]. The 2012 induced-gravitational-collapse paradigm inverts this: the Type Ib/c supernova explodes first and its ejecta, accreting hypercritically onto the NS companion, induce the collapse to a BH that emits the GRB [2012ApJ...758L...7R]. Both are called 'induced' collapse/explosion, but the trigger and the triggered object are swapped.
dossiers.activity: Active continuously from the 1998-2002 dyadosphere/PEM-pulse founding burst [1998A&A...338L..87P, 2000A&A...359..855R, 2001ApJ...555L.113R] through a per-burst fireshell-fitting phase around 2007-2013 [2009A&A...498..501C, 2012A&A...543A..10I, 2013ApJ...772...62M], peaking around the median year 2015 with the IGC/BdHN reformation [2012ApJ...758L...7R, 2014ApJ...793L..36F, 2016ApJ...832..136R]; still producing new machinery (X-ray flare analysis, inner-engine GeV modeling, afterglow morphology) through 2018-2021 [2018ApJ...852...53R, 2019ApJ...886...82R, 2021MNRAS.504.5301R], so the community remains active at the corpus edge, now centered on the BdHN taxonomy rather than the original dyadosphere.

dossiers.name: Indirect Dark Matter Detection
dossiers.defining_problem: Whether dark matter can be detected indirectly through the gamma-ray and positron-annihilation photons its particle annihilations produce — in the Galactic center, the Galactic bulge, dwarf spheroidals, and the cosmological extragalactic background — and, critically, whether observed high-energy anomalies (the EGRET Galactic-center source [2004APh....21..267C], the HESS TeV signal [2005PhRvL..94m1301B], the INTEGRAL/SPI 511 keV bulge line [2004PhRvL..92j1301B], and the Fermi 1-3 GeV Galactic-center excess [2014PhRvL.113o1302F]) are annihilating dark matter or conventional astrophysics. The community sits inside the GRB corpus because GRBs/hypernovae in the Galactic center are the leading astrophysical competitor for the positron budget behind the 511 keV line [2004ApJ...602L..17C, 2005A&A...432..889P, 2006PhLB..636...20B].
populations_events: The EGRET gamma-ray source at the Galactic center, whose spectrum is compatible with WIMP annihilation [2004APh....21..267C]
The INTEGRAL/SPI 511 keV positron-annihilation line from the Galactic bulge, extended, bulge-shaped, with no high-energy or 26Al counterpart [2004PhRvL..92j1301B, 2004ApJ...602L..17C]
The HESS TeV gamma-ray signal from the Galactic-center direction [2005PhRvL..94m1301B]
The Fermi 1-3 GeV Galactic-center excess [2014PhRvL.113o1302F]
Milky Way dwarf spheroidal satellites (Sagittarius, Draco, the combined 15-dSph sample) as clean dark-matter targets [2004PhRvL..93p1302H, 2015PhRvL.115w1301A]
GRB-associated Type Ic hypernovae (SN 2003dh-like) in the Galactic center as candidate positron injectors [2004ApJ...602L..17C]
The neutron-star population of the Galactic bulge, used to bound Kaluza-Klein graviton decay [2004PhRvL..92k1102C]
Unresolved blazars ('grazars') as the astrophysical background to the extragalactic gamma-ray signal [1994ApJ...430L..21S]
instruments_datasets: INTEGRAL/SPI 511 keV spectroscopy and spatial mapping of the Galactic bulge [2004PhRvL..92j1301B, 2004ApJ...602L..17C, 2009PhRvL.103c1301L]
EGRET catalog data: the Galactic-center source and blazar/diffuse-background measurements [2004APh....21..267C, 1994ApJ...430L..21S, 2005PhRvL..94q1301B]
COMPTEL diffuse gamma-ray constraints [2005PhRvL..94q1301B]
HESS atmospheric Cherenkov TeV observations of the Galactic center [2005PhRvL..94m1301B]

GLAST/Fermi-LAT, first as the anticipated discriminator [2002PhRvD..66l3502U, 2004APh....21..267C], then delivering six-year Pass8 dwarf-spheroidal limits [2015PhRvL.115w1301A] and the GeV Galactic-center excess [2014PhRvL.113o1302F]
characteristic_methods: Analytical particle-physics computation of annihilation spectra, including full one-loop calculations of line channels (chi chi -> Z gamma, 2 gamma) in the MSSM [1998PhRvD..57.1962U] and internal-bremsstrahlung radiative corrections [2005PhRvL..94m1301B, 2005PhRvL..94q1301B]
Dark-matter halo-profile modeling (NFW, Kravtsov, minicusps, black-hole spikes) to set the annihilation flux normalization [1998PhRvD..57.1962U, 2004PhRvL..93f1302G, 2014PhRvL.113o1302F]
N-body-simulation-calibrated structure-formation modeling of the cosmological annihilation signal [2002PhRvD..66l3502U]
Relic-density (thermal freeze-out) consistency checks on proposed candidates [2004PhRvL..92j1301B, 2005PhRvL..94m1301B]

Rate/budget accounting: comparing positron injection rates from candidate sources (hypernovae, GRB pair leakage, SNe Ia) against the annihilation rate implied by the 511 keV flux [2004ApJ...602L..17C, 2006PhLB..636...20B, 2005A&A...432..889P]
Spectral and angular signature fitting to telescope data, and stacked/population upper limits (15 combined dwarfs) [2004APh....21..267C, 2015PhRvL.115w1301A]
recurring_models: Supersymmetric neutralino (LSP) WIMP dark matter, including mSUGRA and pure-Higgsino limits [2002PhRvD..66l3502U, 1998PhRvD..57.1962U, 2004APh....21..267C]
Light (1-100 MeV) annihilating dark matter as the source of Galactic-bulge positrons [2004PhRvL..92j1301B, 2004PhRvL..93p1302H]
Kaluza-Klein dark matter and large-extra-dimension gravitons from TeV-scale extra dimensions [2005PhRvL..94m1301B, 2004PhRvL..92k1102C]

Characteristic annihilation spectral signatures: pi0 continuum with a sharp cutoff at the WIMP mass and monochromatic lines redshift-smeared into asymmetric bumps [2002PhRvD..66l3502U]; flat internal-bremsstrahlung spectra with abrupt mass cutoffs [2005PhRvL..94m1301B]
Inner-halo density enhancements and their dynamics: the r^-3/2 stellar-scattering minicusp around Sgr A* [2004PhRvL..93f1302G] and adiabatic black-hole spikes [2014PhRvL.113o1302F]

Astrophysical positron-source alternatives: bipolar hypernova 56Ni ejection with polar positron escape [2004ApJ...602L..17C], GRB pair leakage and photon pair-production in molecular clouds [2006PhLB..636...20B], CMZ mini-starburst GRBs with bulge-wide positron diffusion [2005A&A...432..889P], and nucleosynthetic beta+ decay with extensive propagation [2009PhRvL.103c1301L]
shaping_results: Srednicki, Theisen & Silk showed halo WIMP annihilation into quarkonium plus a monochromatic photon could produce observable sharp gamma-ray peaks — the founding line-signature idea [1986PhRvL..56..263S]
Full one-loop MSSM calculation of neutralino annihilation to Z gamma established the two-line (2gamma + Zgamma) diagnostic of the WIMP's nature [1998PhRvD..57.1962U]

The community founder computed the cosmological WIMP annihilation contribution to the extragalactic gamma-ray background, with pi0 cutoff and redshift-smeared line bumps detectable by GLAST [2002PhRvD..66l3502U], against the blazar background quantified from EGRET [1994ApJ...430L..21S]
Boehm et al. proposed the INTEGRAL 511 keV bulge emission as 1-100 MeV dark matter annihilation consistent with the relic density — the result that ignited the 2004-2005 burst [2004PhRvL..92j1301B]
Cassé et al. countered that ~0.02 SN 2003dh-like GRB/hypernovae per century in the Galactic center suffice for the positron flux, tying the problem to GRB astrophysics [2004ApJ...602L..17C]
Internal bremsstrahlung from 'invisible' annihilation violates COMPTEL/EGRET unless the dark matter mass is below ~20 MeV, sharply squeezing the MeV window [2005PhRvL..94q1301B]

The EGRET Galactic-center source shown compatible with WIMP annihilation, with GLAST as arbiter [2004APh....21..267C]; the HESS TeV signal fit by ~1-10 TeV Kaluza-Klein dark matter [2005PhRvL..94m1301B]
Stellar scattering off the Sgr A* cluster drives the inner-parsec profile to a universal r^-3/2 minicusp, fixing the Galactic-center flux prediction [2004PhRvL..93f1302G]
Six years of Fermi-LAT Pass8 data on 15 dwarf spheroidals yielded no detection and pushed limits below the thermal relic cross section for masses below ~100 GeV [2015PhRvL.115w1301A]
internal_disagreements: The 1986 quarkonium-line rate dispute: Rich showed the Srednicki-Theisen-Silk calculation [1986PhRvL..56..263S] 'seriously overestimates' the annihilation-to-quarkonium rate by an order of magnitude or more by neglecting the quarkonium bound-state structure [1986PhRvL..56.2128R]

Origin of the 511 keV bulge positrons — the community's central fight: MeV dark matter annihilation [2004PhRvL..92j1301B, 2004PhRvL..93p1302H] versus GRB/hypernova astrophysics [2004ApJ...602L..17C, 2005A&A...432..889P]; the GRB-leakage variant itself found only 'marginally consistent', needing above-average GRB rates or molecular-cloud optical depths [2006PhLB..636...20B]

Whether MeV dark matter survives its own gamma rays: internal bremsstrahlung violates COMPTEL/EGRET unless m < ~20 MeV [2005PhRvL..94q1301B], directly constraining the 1-100 MeV window claimed by [2004PhRvL..92j1301B]

Whether the 511 keV morphology is dark-matter evidence at all: Lingenfelter et al. argued that with realistic positron propagation, standard nucleosynthetic beta+ sources fully reproduce the spatial distribution and ~97% positronium fraction, 'leaving no new signal for dark matter to explain' [2009PhRvL.103c1301L] — against the dark-matter reading of the same map [2004PhRvL..92j1301B]

The black-hole-spike tension: if the Fermi GeV excess is dark matter, a canonical adiabatic spike around Sgr A* would outshine it 35-fold and is disfavored by the data, contradicting the standard spike-formation picture unless Galactic history was non-adiabatic [2014PhRvL.113o1302F] (compare the milder minicusp of [2004PhRvL..93f1302G])
dossiers.activity: Seeded in 1986 with the quarkonium gamma-ray line idea [1986PhRvL..56..263S, 1986PhRvL..56.2128R] and built through 1990s loop calculations [1998PhRvD..57.1962U] and the 2002 cosmological-signal paper [2002PhRvD..66l3502U], the community exploded in 2004-2005 around the INTEGRAL 511 keV line, the EGRET Galactic-center source, and the HESS TeV signal (most of the locally influential papers date to those two years; median year 2007). A second, Fermi-era wave ran through 2009-2015 on the GeV Galactic-center excess and dwarf-spheroidal limits [2014PhRvL.113o1302F, 2015PhRvL.115w1301A]. Within this GRB corpus it is now largely dormant: no influential member paper postdates 2015, the MeV-dark-matter reading of the 511 keV line having been squeezed by gamma-ray constraints [2005PhRvL..94q1301B] and propagation arguments [2009PhRvL.103c1301L], and the WIMP program left holding sub-thermal-relic upper limits [2015PhRvL.115w1301A].

dossiers.name: Terrestrial and astrobiological effects of GRBs
dossiers.defining_problem: What a Galactic gamma-ray burst would do to the Earth (and to habitable planets generally): how often a burst close enough to matter occurs, how its ionizing photons deposit energy in an atmosphere, how the resulting NOx chemistry depletes ozone and admits biologically lethal solar UVB, and whether any event in the geological or historical record — above all the Late Ordovician mass extinction ~440-445 Myr ago and the AD 774/5 radiocarbon spike — can be attributed to one. The founding paper [1995ApJ...444L..53T] posed the problem the moment BATSE made GRBs cosmological: if bursts occur in normal galaxies, one strikes our Galaxy every 1e5-1e6 yr, its gamma-ray flux dwarfing the largest solar flares, driving stratospheric NO production, multi-year ozone loss, and possibly anomalous radionuclide traces. The community then quantified the rate per galaxy [2002ApJ...566..723S], the atmospheric response in detail [2005ApJ...622L.153T; 2005ApJ...634..509T; 2005GeoRL..3214808M; 2007ApJ...654..373E], the Ordovician-extinction hypothesis [2004IJAsB...3...55M; 2009Pbio...35..311M], and the generalization to exoplanet atmospheres, the Galactic Habitable Zone, and the Fermi paradox [2004Icar..171..229S; 1999JBIS...52...19A; 2014PhRvL.113w1102P; 2021A&A...647A..41S].
populations_events: Hypothetical nearby Galactic GRBs within ~2 kpc of Earth, estimated to occur at least once per Gyr [2005ApJ...622L.153T], or two or more dangerously near events per Gyr [2004IJAsB...3...55M]
The Late Ordovician mass extinction (~440-445 Myr ago), the community's flagship candidate GRB-initiated extinction [2004IJAsB...3...55M; 2005ApJ...634..509T; 2009Pbio...35..311M]

The AD 774/5 rapid 14C increase in tree rings (7e24 erg gamma-ray energy input at Earth), attributed to a Galactic short GRB at 1-4 kpc [2013MNRAS.430...32H] or to a solar particle event [2013NatCo...4.1748M; 2018NatCo...9.3495U]
The second rapid 14C event of AD 992-993 with matching 10Be signature [2013NatCo...4.1748M]
Low-metallicity long-GRB host galaxies at z<=0.25, all with 12+log(O/H)<8.6 [2006AcA....56..333S]
Short-hard GRBs as a local threat comparable to supernovae and exceeding long bursts [2011AsBio..11..343M; 2007ApJ...654..373E]
Terrestrial-like exoplanets in the habitable zone, receiving GRB/SN fluences of 1e6-1e9 erg/cm^2 at ~100 events per Gyr [2004Icar..171..229S]
The Galactic-position-dependent population of habitable planets (Galactic Habitable Zone) [2014PhRvL.113w1102P; 2021A&A...647A..41S]
instruments_datasets: BATSE/CGRO isotropy and intensity distributions, the observational trigger for the founding cosmological-distance argument [1995ApJ...444L..53T]
Local GRB rate and peak-luminosity estimates (Schmidt) combined with cosmic star-formation-rate history [2002ApJ...566..723S]
Tree-ring 14C series and Antarctic ice-core 10Be flux records for AD 774/5 and AD 992/3 [2013NatCo...4.1748M; 2013MNRAS.430...32H]
Sub-annual earlywood/latewood 14C measurements in Arctic tree rings across latitudes [2018NatCo...9.3495U]
SDSS star-forming-galaxy census and emission-line oxygen abundances of low-z GRB hosts [2006AcA....56..333S]
BATSE/Swift GRB luminosity functions and rate evolution used for lethality statistics [2014PhRvL.113w1102P]
Late Ordovician paleontological geographic extinction patterns from the fossil record [2009Pbio...35..311M]
Auger Observatory anticipated as the test of the GRB origin of ~1e18 eV cosmic rays [2005ApJ...628L..21D]
characteristic_methods: Atmospheric photochemistry modeling of impulsive gamma-ray energy deposition: NO/NO2 production, catalytic ozone destruction, and multi-year recovery, in 1D and 2D models [1995ApJ...444L..53T; 2005ApJ...622L.153T; 2005ApJ...634..509T; 2007ApJ...654..373E]

Scaling cosmological GRB rates to a per-galaxy or per-blue-luminosity rate, then to the probability of a burst within a lethal distance of Earth [2002ApJ...566..723S; 2005ApJ...622L.153T; 2014PhRvL.113w1102P]
Monte Carlo radiative transfer of ionizing photons (Compton scattering + photoabsorption) through model atmospheres of varying column density [2004Icar..171..229S]
DNA-damage and UVB-dose estimation from computed ozone depletion, extrapolated from modern-organism sensitivity [2005ApJ...634..509T; 2005ApJ...622L.153T]
Radiative-transfer and climate-impact estimation of NO2 visible opacity as a glaciation trigger [2005GeoRL..3214808M]

Cosmogenic-isotope energy budgets: converting 14C and 10Be production ratios into source spectra and energies to discriminate GRB, supernova, and solar-flare origins [2013MNRAS.430...32H; 2014AN....335..949N; 2018NatCo...9.3495U]
3D simulations of GRB-accelerated cosmic-ray propagation in the Galactic magnetic field with pitch-angle scattering [2005ApJ...628L..21D]
Order-of-magnitude timescale comparisons between GRB recurrence and biological-evolution timescales for Fermi-paradox arguments [1999JBIS...52...19A]
Galactic habitability mapping: convolving GRB/SN rates, metallicity gradients, and planet occurrence over galactocentric radius and cosmic time [2014PhRvL.113w1102P; 2021A&A...647A..41S]
Comparison of simulated hemispherical radiation-damage patterns with geographic extinction patterns in the fossil record [2009Pbio...35..311M]
recurring_models: The NOx-catalysis ozone-depletion model: atmospheric absorption of gamma rays dissociates N2, NO/NO2 destroys ozone for years, solar UVB reaching the surface does the biological damage — the community's central causal chain from its founding [1995ApJ...444L..53T] through the detailed calculations [2005ApJ...622L.153T; 2005ApJ...634..509T]

The GRB-Ordovician hypothesis: a burst within ~2 kpc initiating both the UVB extinction pulse and, via NO2 opacity and cooling, the end-Ordovician glaciation [2004IJAsB...3...55M; 2005GeoRL..3214808M; 2005ApJ...634..509T]

Fluence-scaling with duration-insensitivity: atmospheric impact depends on total fluence, nearly independent of burst duration from 0.1 s to 1e8 s, unifying short GRBs, long GRBs, X-ray flashes, and supernovae into one framework [2005ApJ...634..509T; 2007ApJ...654..373E]
The lethal-distance / lethal-fluence model (~100 kJ/m^2 at ~2 kpc benchmark) [2005ApJ...622L.153T; 2014PhRvL.113w1102P]

GRB regulation of the Galactic Habitable Zone and of the timing of intelligence (Fermi-paradox phase transition at mean lethal-event spacing ~1e8 yr) [1999JBIS...52...19A; 2014PhRvL.113w1102P; 2021A&A...647A..41S]
The metallicity aversion of long GRBs (threshold ~0.15 Z_sun), which shields metal-rich galaxies like the Milky Way [2006AcA....56..333S; 2021A&A...647A..41S]
The Galactic short GRB as cause of historical cosmogenic-isotope spikes [2013MNRAS.430...32H]
Atmospheric reprocessing of ionizing radiation into surficial UV on exoplanets, with ~100 g/cm^2 as the gamma-ray blocking column [2004Icar..171..229S]
shaping_results: Thorsett 1995: a Galactic GRB every 1e5-1e6 yr would deliver flux far exceeding the largest solar flares, drive NO-catalyzed ozone loss for years, and possibly leave radionuclide traces — the founding statement of the field [1995ApJ...444L..53T]

Scalo & Wheeler 2002: Milky Way GRB rate 5.5e-7/yr, >6000 SNe Ibc per isotropic-equivalent GRB, and biologically significant irradiation events at ~100-500 per Gyr for planets with thin atmospheres [2002ApJ...566..723S]

Melott et al. 2004: the proposal that the Late Ordovician mass extinction ~440 Myr ago was at least partly GRB-initiated, with dangerously near bursts expected two or more times per Gyr [2004IJAsB...3...55M]

Thomas et al. 2005: first detailed atmospheric computation — a 100 kJ/m^2 burst at 2 kpc gives 35% globally averaged ozone depletion (55% at some latitudes) persisting >5 yr, tripling surface UVB [2005ApJ...622L.153T], extended to 38% global / 74% local depletion, DNA damage up to 16x the annual global average, and ~7 yr recovery [2005ApJ...634..509T]
Melott et al. 2005: NO2 visible opacity reduces surface sunlight by up to a few percent, greatest at the poles — potentially sufficient to initiate the end-Ordovician glaciation [2005GeoRL..3214808M]

Ejzak et al. 2007: atmospheric impact is nearly duration-independent at fixed fluence (0.1 s to 1e8 s) and maximized for spectral peaks up to ~20 MeV, folding short GRBs and supernovae into the same formalism [2007ApJ...654..373E]

Stanek et al. 2006: all five low-z long-GRB hosts have 12+log(O/H)<8.6, implying a ~0.15 Z_sun metallicity ceiling and that the metal-rich Milky Way has been unable to host long GRBs for billions of years [2006AcA....56..333S]

Smith, Scalo & Wheeler 2004: atmospheres >~100 g/cm^2 block gamma rays but reprocess up to 10% of incident energy into surficial UV, defining the exoplanet-atmosphere response to GRB irradiation [2004Icar..171..229S]

Hambaryan & Neuhauser 2013: the AD 774/5 14C spike (7e24 erg at Earth) is consistent with a Galactic short GRB at 1-4 kpc — claimed as the first evidence for a short GRB in our Galaxy [2013MNRAS.430...32H]
Miyake et al. 2013: a second rapid 14C event in AD 992-993 with 14C/10Be proportions matching AD 774/5, arguing both share a common, plausibly solar, origin [2013NatCo...4.1748M]
Uusitalo et al. 2018: latitudinal dependence of the AD 774 14C signal in Arctic tree rings is consistent with a solar particle event and inconsistent with a GRB or supernova [2018NatCo...9.3495U]
Piran & Jimenez 2014: ~50% probability of a lethal GRB within the last 500 Myr, a 95%-lethal inner Galaxy, life confined to ~10% of galaxies, and no Earth-like life at z>0.5 [2014PhRvL.113w1102P]
Melott & Thomas 2011 census: short-hard GRBs are a threat comparable to supernovae and greater than long bursts [2011AsBio..11..343M]
internal_disagreements: The cause of the AD 774/5 radiocarbon spike. Hambaryan & Neuhauser argued a Galactic short GRB at 1-4 kpc is consistent with all observables — the required 7e24 erg within a year, the hard spectrum matching the 14C/10Be production ratio, and the absence of a historical supernova sighting or remnant — calling it the first evidence for a short GRB in our Galaxy, while judging solar and stellar flares unlikely [2013MNRAS.430...32H]; Neuhauser & Hambaryan themselves quantified that an unbeamed solar flare would need ~2000x the Carrington event energy and put the probability of a sufficient super-flare within 3000 yr as low as 0.008-0.3 [2014AN....335..949N]. Against this, Miyake et al. found a second, comparable 14C event in AD 992-993 with the same 14C/10Be proportions, arguing the recurrence rate favors a solar origin over an extraterrestrial one [2013NatCo...4.1748M], and Uusitalo et al. showed the AD 774 signal has a strong poleward latitudinal dependence that a solar particle event produces but a GRB or supernova cannot [2018NatCo...9.3495U].

Whether the Milky Way can host the long GRBs the extinction scenarios require. The Ordovician and ozone-depletion calculations assume the Galactic long-GRB rate scales from cosmological rates, giving at least one burst within 2 kpc per Gyr [2005ApJ...622L.153T; 2004IJAsB...3...55M; 1995ApJ...444L..53T]. Stanek et al. countered that long GRBs trace only low-metallicity star formation (ceiling ~0.15 Z_sun) and that the Milky Way has been too metal-rich to host them for at least the last several billion years, explicitly flagging the implication for GRB mass-extinction claims [2006AcA....56..333S]. Piran & Jimenez, assuming host-metallicity bias does not significantly alter the Galactic rate, nonetheless kept a 50% probability of a lethal GRB in the last 500 Myr [2014PhRvL.113w1102P].

Where in the Galaxy life is safest from GRBs. Piran & Jimenez concluded the inner Milky Way (within 4 kpc of the center) has a 95% probability of lethal GRB irradiation and only regions beyond 10 kpc drop below 50% [2014PhRvL.113w1102P]; Spinelli & Ghirlanda, folding in the metallicity aversion of long GRBs and planet density, concluded the opposite geometry for the recent Galaxy — the 2-8 kpc band has been the safest for the last 4 Gyr while the low-metallicity outer Milky Way was sterilized by 2-5 long GRBs in the last 500 Myr [2021A&A...647A..41S].

Which burst class dominates the local threat. The founding line of work centered on long/cosmological bursts and their Galactic analogs [1995ApJ...444L..53T; 2005ApJ...622L.153T], and Piran & Jimenez ranked long GRBs as the most dangerous type by energy and rate [2014PhRvL.113w1102P]; the Melott & Thomas census instead ranked short-hard bursts as a substantial threat comparable to supernovae and greater than the higher-luminosity long bursts [2011AsBio..11..343M], a shift enabled by the duration-insensitivity result of Ejzak et al. [2007ApJ...654..373E].
dossiers.activity: Founded in 1995 with Thorsett's BATSE-era warning [1995ApJ...444L..53T], quantified in 1999-2004 [1999JBIS...52...19A; 2002ApJ...566..723S; 2004Icar..171..229S], and peaking in an intense 2004-2007 wave of Ordovician-extinction and atmospheric-modeling papers from the Melott-Thomas collaboration [2004IJAsB...3...55M; 2005ApJ...622L.153T; 2005ApJ...634..509T; 2005GeoRL..3214808M; 2007ApJ...654..373E]. A second burst of activity around 2013-2018 followed the AD 774/5 radiocarbon controversy [2013MNRAS.430...32H; 2013NatCo...4.1748M; 2014AN....335..949N; 2018NatCo...9.3495U] and the cosmological-habitability turn [2014PhRvL.113w1102P] — consistent with the community's median year of 2012.5. It remains modestly active into the 2020s, now oriented toward Galactic and exoplanetary habitability rather than new Earth-effect calculations [2021A&A...647A..41S].

dossiers.name: Quark-Star GRB Central Engines
dossiers.defining_problem: Whether the deconfinement of quark matter in compact stars — collisions of strange stars [1991ApJ...375..209H], accretion- or spin-down-induced conversion of neutron stars to strange/quark stars [1996PhRvL..77.1210C; 1996ApJ...462L..63M; 2000ApJ...530L..69B], or delayed nucleation of a quark core in a metastable hadronic star [2003ApJ...586.1250B; 2004ApJ...614..314B] — can supply the energy (10^50–10^53 erg), the low baryon loading, and the event rate required to power cosmological gamma-ray bursts, and how such events would connect to supernovae and to observable compact-star populations [2000A&A...357..543W; 2016PhRvD..94h3010L].
populations_events: Cosmological GRB population and its rate (~10^-6/yr/galaxy) matched to quark-star formation rates [1996ApJ...462L..63M; 1996PhRvL..77.1210C]
BATSE weak-burst source counts used to constrain strange-star origins [1991ApJ...375..209H; 1994A&A...286L..17K]
The 5 March 1979 gamma-ray transient, the community's founding event [1986PhRvL..57.2088A; 1987PhRvL..58.2152A]
GRB 990705 and GRB 011211, the delayed SN-GRB cases explained by delayed quark-matter collapse [2003ApJ...586.1250B; 2002A&A...390L..39O]
SN 1998bw and the supernova/GRB connection [2000A&A...357..543W]
Neutron stars in low-mass X-ray binaries as conversion progenitors [1996PhRvL..77.1210C]
Short GRBs with internal X-ray plateaus, ~22% supramassive-remnant fraction from Swift data [2016PhRvD..94h3010L]
The bimodal short/long GRB duration distribution, mapped to two engine regimes (~2 s and ~81 s) [2002A&A...387..725O]
instruments_datasets: BATSE/Compton GRO angular distribution and source-count statistics of weak bursts [1991ApJ...375..209H; 1994A&A...286L..17K]
Swift X-ray afterglow light curves of short GRBs (internal plateaus and break times) [2016PhRvD..94h3010L]
X-ray spectra of compact sources used for mass-radius extraction [2004ApJ...614..314B]
Gravitational-wave temporal signatures proposed to discriminate quark-star formation from NS mergers [1996ApJ...462L..63M]
characteristic_methods: Analytic energy-budget calculations of the binding-energy release in NS-to-strange-star conversion using competing equations of state [2000ApJ...530L..69B; 1996PhRvL..77.1210C]
Nucleation theory with finite-size/surface-tension effects to compute quark-matter drop formation times and stellar metastability lifetimes [2003ApJ...586.1250B; 2004ApJ...614..314B]
Fireball dynamics and baryon-loading estimates exploiting the bare strange-star surface (Lorentz factors 100 to >5x10^3) [1996PhRvL..77.1210C; 2000A&A...357..543W]
1D numerical hydrodynamic simulation of phase-transition-induced collapse with realistic neutrino physics and fine surface zoning [1998ApJ...501..780F]
Order-of-magnitude burst-rate estimation from stellar evolution and spin-down timescales [1996ApJ...462L..63M; 1991ApJ...375..209H]
Monte Carlo population synthesis of SGRB observables over NS and QS equation-of-state families [2016PhRvD..94h3010L]
Source-count statistics combined with strangelet-contamination arguments to exclude models [1994A&A...286L..17K]
recurring_models: Bodmer-Witten hypothesis that strange quark matter is the absolutely stable ground state of matter, prerequisite of the whole community [1994A&A...286L..17K; 1996PhRvL..77.1210C]
Strange-star collision model for extragalactic GRBs [1991ApJ...375..209H]
Accretion-induced NS-to-strange-star conversion in LMXBs producing a clean fireball [1996PhRvL..77.1210C; 2000ApJ...530L..69B]
Spin-down-triggered quark-core phase transition / super-giant glitch [1996ApJ...462L..63M; 2000A&A...357..543W]

Delayed collapse of a metastable hadronic star via quark-matter nucleation, explaining SN-GRB time delays (the two-step / two-families scenario) [2003ApJ...586.1250B; 2004ApJ...614..314B; 2016EPJA...52...41D]
Quark-Nova: core collapse to a quark star with envelope ejection, up to 10^53 erg [2002A&A...390L..39O]
Color-superconducting (2SC / CFL) quark-star surfaces as photon-fireball generators [2002A&A...387..725O]
Differentially rotating strange stars becoming millisecond pulsars after the burst [1998PhRvL..81.4301D]
Supramassive fast-rotating quark stars as short-GRB postmerger remnants [2016PhRvD..94h3010L]
shaping_results: Strange-star collisions release ~10^50 erg in gamma rays over 0.2 s, detectable to ~1 Gpc — the founding quantitative claim [1991ApJ...375..209H]
Alcock, Farhi & Olinto's strange-star model for the 5 March 1979 transient seeded the field [1986PhRvL..57.2088A; 1987PhRvL..58.2152A]
NS-to-strange-star conversion in LMXBs yields GRB-scale energy with Lorentz factors >5x10^3 from low baryon contamination [1996PhRvL..77.1210C]
Kluzniak's exclusion: strangelet contamination plus BATSE source counts rule out strange-star disruption as the GRB source [1994A&A...286L..17K]
Fryer & Woosley's simulations: phase-transition collapse gives <10^46 erg in material with Gamma>40 and 0.01 Msun of baryon-rich ejecta — far too dirty and weak for GRBs [1998ApJ...501..780F]
Bombaci & Datta: conversion liberates (1-4)x10^53 erg, an order of magnitude above earlier estimates, reviving the engine's energetics [2000ApJ...530L..69B]
Surface tension delays quark-matter nucleation, letting the collapse occur days-to-years after the supernova and explaining GRB 990705 and GRB 011211 [2003ApJ...586.1250B]
Quark deconfinement with finite-size effects makes massive NSs metastable, tying the limiting mass of compact stars to a two-step SN-then-GRB process [2004ApJ...614..314B]
Quark-star equations of state reproduce the narrow break-time distribution of internal X-ray plateaus in Swift short GRBs better than NS EoSs [2016PhRvD..94h3010L]
internal_disagreements: Can strange stars power GRBs at all? Haensel et al. proposed strange-star collisions as the least speculative extragalactic GRB engine [1991ApJ...375..209H], and Cheng & Dai argued conversion events satisfy all cosmological GRB requirements [1996PhRvL..77.1210C]; Kluzniak countered that strangelet release from any strange-star disruption, combined with BATSE source-count statistics, excludes strange stars as sources of the observed bursts [1994A&A...286L..17K].

Clean versus dirty fireballs: analytic models claimed the bare strange-star surface yields very low baryon contamination with Lorentz factors of ~100 to >5x10^3 [1996PhRvL..77.1210C; 2000A&A...357..543W], but Fryer & Woosley's numerical collapse simulations found the ejecta are far too baryon-rich (~0.01 Msun) with <10^46 erg at Gamma>40 — too little to explain GRBs [1998ApJ...501..780F].

Conversion energy budget: early estimates put the phase-transition energy at ~10^52 erg [1996ApJ...462L..63M], while Bombaci & Datta computed (1-4)x10^53 erg and explicitly flagged it as an order of magnitude larger than previous estimates [2000ApJ...530L..69B].

Where the fireball is made: Ouyed & Sannino generate the fireball from unstable 2SC particles at an existing quark-star surface, an approach they present as fundamentally different from models where the fireball is generated during the collapse or conversion itself [2002A&A...387..725O vs 1996PhRvL..77.1210C; 2000ApJ...530L..69B].
dossiers.activity: Founded by the 1986-1987 strange-star interpretation of the 5 March 1979 transient [1986PhRvL..57.2088A; 1987PhRvL..58.2152A] and Haensel's 1991 collision model [1991ApJ...375..209H], the community was most active from the mid-1990s BATSE era through the mid-2000s (conversion, quark-nova, and delayed-collapse models, 1996-2004; median year 2006). It has since narrowed but persists: the multimessenger era repurposed the same physics for short-GRB remnants and the two-families scenario, with active work in 2016 on supramassive quark stars from Swift internal plateaus [2016PhRvD..94h3010L] and hadronic-to-quark transitions in explosive phenomena [2016EPJA...52...41D].
